Audit and pin one exact sandraschi Blender MCP revision before any benchmark execution or installation.

## Owned output
A reviewed pin record containing upstream repository and commit/tag, immutable source/archive hash, license files, dependency lock, supported Blender/Python versions, install method, commands/tools exposed, process and filesystem behavior, network/telemetry behavior, arbitrary-code surfaces, known vulnerabilities/issues, and rollback/removal steps.

Do not install the MCP, follow floating branches, approve network downloads at runtime, or infer safety from popularity.

## Acceptance criteria

- Review traces command dispatch, subprocesses, Python execution, file read/write scope, environment/secrets access, network endpoints, telemetry, dependency scripts, and update behavior.
- A sandbox/isolated-profile plan names allowlisted operations/paths and denied behaviors.
- Pin includes checksums, exact reproduction commands, reviewer, date, unresolved risks, expiry/re-review triggers, and accept/reject recommendation.
- Any unbounded code execution or unclear license/network behavior blocks use until explicitly resolved.

## Method

1. Bind the exact accepted Level 2 revision and freeze its reset/hash/order/ABI observations. Re-measure duplicate authority and current code geometry; older research measurements are hypotheses, not source truth.
2. Emit a serial fold chain with one real code transition per leaf: state lifetime/reset schema; terrain owner; source arena/identity; RNG owner; ordered effect journal; literal source scheduler including `runagain`; static source-keyed dispatch; descriptor-driven selection/Unity manifest only where the accepted revision still needs each transition. Pure moves and semantic changes are separate. Level 1 stays behind its sealed adapter unless an explicit equivalence experiment is later authorized.
3. Export/validate Level 3 and enumerate its complete reachable content and behavior delta: map/terrain facts, spawns/families, spells/effects, objectives/triggers, buildings/economy, required source facts, assets/audio/HUD and route integration.
4. Map every row to an existing capability using dispatch phase/site, class/action, and required model/subtype context. Reuse is a checked claim, not a name match.
5. For every unsupported semantic, use independent frontier architecture/research models, preserve dissent and falsifiers, and define the smallest honest authority seam. Oracle cross-examines consequential decisions. Source and executable evidence decide; agreement is advisory.
6. Create family/system aggregation parents and Luna-Max-sized implementation children only where the measured delta demands work. Every leaf names inputs, disjoint owned surface, canonical carriers it borrows, positive observable, discriminating negative, exact focused verification and No-Claim. Parents do not become dispatch keys or authorities; ABI/Unity work remains a projection lane.
7. Create one Level 3 composition/qualification parent depending on the required fold and capability leaves. Create no per-level session/API, duplicate matrix, dashboard, plugin/ECS/DSL or placeholder.
8. Mark the shared-seam frontier explicit. Keep Level 4 deferred until CampaignState lifetimes, arena identity, scheduler continuation, dispatch-key shape, SourceFacts, objective vocabulary, and campaign selection/ABI are either frozen or owned by a blocking leaf.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The fold graph is revision-bound, serial only where one canonical carrier is touched, and each leaf is an independently landable behavior-preserving code change with an old/new observation relation.
- [ ] Delta denominator is complete for the qualified Level 3 package or each exclusion is mechanical.
- [ ] Existing handlers/systems are reused unchanged wherever their source/context contract matches.
- [ ] Every new Bead is independently landable by one Luna-Max writer and advances a playable Level 3 route; no per-action grazing or process-only leaves.
- [ ] Dependencies encode real data/authority ordering; disjoint families/systems form parallel tracks and shared spine edits have one owner.
- [ ] Level 3 boots via the generic campaign selector/ABI plan; no `Level3ResetSession`, `mc_native_level3_*`, scattered `level == 3` gameplay branches, placeholder or speculative framework is proposed.
- [ ] The deferred Level 4 planner dependency is confirmed and its safe overlap frontier is explicit.

## No-claim

This planning closure proves only the declared fold/delta accounting and executable work graph. It does not prove the fold, Level 3 behavior, playability, or cross-level handler equivalence.

title: [L2] Carry source player-state byte 0x006 for type-3 banishment
description:
## Deliverable
Add a versioned, source-backed Level 2 carrier for `array_0x2BDE[color].byte_0x006`, so Nyphur terminal lifecycle and objective type 3 can distinguish an active opponent from permanent banishment without aliasing the compact player record.

## Exact source and production consumer
At pinned remc2 `6806c7204d17220ecc0430759f784aea8ee2ddb2`, compact `players.bin` bytes `record[6..8]` encode little-endian `ActPlayerIndex`; they are not the banishment byte. The lethal path is `sub_12A70` -> lethal `sub_5EFA0` -> action 2 `sub_5E310` -> action 3 `sub_5E7C0`, which clears `array_0x2BDE[victim_color].byte_0x006` on permanent banishment; objective type 3 consumes that byte. This leaf owns only the lossless package/carrier contract required by that production chain. Runtime mutation, respawn, denominator correction, and objective behavior remain in `mc-2eby.1`.

## Versioned package contract
Current owner manifest v4 pins `players.bin` component v3 / 662-byte records. Do not silently redefine v4. Add owner manifest schema v5 with the same typed Level 2 member set and normalization as v4 but `players.bin` component v4 / 663-byte records. Preserve owner v4 + component v3 as the prior inspection contract; qualified type-3 production requires v5 + component v4. Preserve the existing `Type_str_164` auxiliary beginning at record offset 573 (`0x23d`) and append the banishment byte at record offset 662 (`0x296`). Update qualified package, closure, cache, and indexed-frame identities through their established versioned paths; no regenerated identity may be accepted without semantic positive/negative review.

## Ownership
One Luna-Max writer owns the coherent package migration:
- `research/private/remc2-level-exporter/src/exporter_main.cpp`
- `research/private/remc2-level-exporter/tests/verify_package.py`
- `research/private/remc2-level-exporter/tests/test_exporter_cli.py`
- `research/private/remc2-level-exporter/tests/test_verifier.py`
- `research/private/remc2-level-asset-closure/build_closure.py`
- `research/private/remc2-level-asset-closure/tests/test_closure.py`
- `research/private/remc2-unity-asset-cache/build_cache.py`
- `research/private/remc2-unity-asset-cache/tests/test_cache.py`
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-core/src/day_indexed_frame.rs`
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-core/src/native_world.rs`

Do not edit remc2, the C ABI, Unity C#, Level 1, denominator data, Nyphur terminal policy, or objective policy.

## Acceptance
- Fresh qualified Level 2 export writes exact source values in owner-v5/component-v4 663-byte records; manifest descriptors and hashes bind the new byte.
- Owner v4/component v3 remains valid only for its existing inspection contract and fails closed for the qualified type-3 production session; v2/573, missing, truncated, duplicate, wrong-version, wrong-profile, member-set drift, and descriptor mismatch create no partial session.
- Closure/cache/indexed-frame consumers explicitly admit v5 and preserve v4 behavior; generated identities change only because the source-backed member changed.
- Rust parses the new byte into authoritative mutable player state, keeps `record[6..8]` as `ActPlayerIndex`, includes the byte in reset/replay/hash, and exposes no inferred default or test-only setter.
- Focused exporter, closure, cache, indexed-frame, and sim-core tests prove exact offsets, both byte values, schema-version separation, malformed inputs, reset/replay, and hash discrimination. Run the Level 2 profile guard, format, focused correctness/suspicious Clippy, and each affected owner-data suite.

## Positive observable
A qualified owner-v5 Level 2 session reports the exact exported banishment byte independently of `ActPlayerIndex`; reset/replay restores its initial value and campaign hash.

## Planted negatives
Changing only compact `record[6..8]` never changes the banishment carrier. An owner-v4/component-v3 package cannot be laundered into type-3 production evidence. A v5 manifest paired with a v3/662 member, or v4 paired with v4/663, fails closed.

## No claim
This leaf does not implement lethal damage, score award, action 2/3 dispatch, holder release, respawn, objective advancement, or denominator mutation. Those remain open in `mc-2eby.1` and its declared dependencies.

title: Build the frozen-feature manifest closure validator and evidence schema
description:
## Outcome
Build the deterministic validator used by the final feature-completeness gate to prove that every row in the approved original-product manifest has implementation and evidence coverage.

## Inputs
Approved roadmap and feature-ledger schemas; spell, creature, campaign, asset, audio, UI, runtime-target, provenance, and contract-to-test schemas; synthetic positive and deliberately invalid fixtures.

## Owned output
A versioned machine-readable closure schema, validator, canonical command, synthetic fixture suite, JSON/JUnit report format, and documented integration point for mc-4iqb.

## Non-goals
This bead does not claim the product is feature complete, execute the final production audit, implement missing rows, or silently waive gaps. mc-4iqb runs the validator against the frozen production manifest only after its other implementation and evidence dependencies complete.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each manifest row must map to stable implementation bead IDs, focused test IDs, integration gates, provenance records, runtime targets, contract versions, and immutable evidence locations.
- Duplicate owners, orphan implementation beads, stale versions, forbidden fixtures, missing runtime coverage, missing evidence, expired waivers, and newly introduced unmapped rows fail closed.
- Waivers require reason, player impact, approver, milestone, expiry/review point, containment, and replacement plan.
- Synthetic fixtures prove every failure class and one complete passing manifest.

Run the exact hash-registered owned MC2 build in two or more isolated DOSBox instances and produce a private, repeatable network-observation corpus for rules that the manual does not establish. Cross-check black-box results with bounded Ghidra analysis only after observations and after mc-51m accepts the reproducible lab.

## Questions
- Repeatable session discovery, same-session admission, wizard/colour/level selection, player-slot limits, start and leave behavior.
- Direct/AoE spell interactions against self, opposing wizard, castle, carrier, controlled/neutral creature, mana, terrain and water; test the Alliance spell separately without assuming player teams.
- Death with/without a surviving castle, castle destruction, respawn/rebuild, permanent elimination, observation state and disconnect.
- Independently vary wizard death, castle destruction, mana control, scripted/creature objectives and time to identify or falsify victory, loss, exit, quota, tie and stalemate predicates.
- Inventory selectable network levels, initial entities/markers/exits/objectives/ecology and player-count-dependent changes without copying level geometry or assets.
- Verify that network play continues while map/message/menu affordances are open.

## Method and provenance
Record executable/install/config hashes, per-instance Environment and Calibration IDs, DOSBox version/cycles/timing, topology/role, clock mapping, latency/jitter/loss/reordering, selected level/slots, exact input script, independent resets/repetitions and synchronized private captures. Use Ghidra only after mc-51m to cross-check relation/damage filters, death transitions, victory/exit activation and network objective loading. Keep raw video, screenshots, addresses, symbols, pseudocode, tables and original data in the private lab. Transfer only reviewed independent state machines, invariants, evidence axes, falsified hypotheses and synthetic vectors.

## Acceptance
1. Two-instance entry is reproducible from a fresh isolated configuration without distributing original files.
2. Relationship/damage observations cover self and opponent across every demo-critical target class and distinguish direct, area, terrain and world effects.
3. Death/rebuild/elimination/disconnect states are reproduced with and without an eligible stronghold.
4. The smallest observed terminal/victory/exit trigger is reported alongside falsified alternatives; unknowns remain explicit.
5. Each selectable network-level family is classified for objectives, exit, ecology and player-count behavior without copied geometry/expression.
6. Every accepted high-confidence discrete rule has at least three independently reset matching valid repetitions, a boundary/negative case and a materially independent Ghidra/runtime corroboration route; timing/stochastic rules follow the protocol stopping rule.
7. The output directly feeds mc-pj9e, mc-rj3a and mc-pv9s; no original payload enters their public-safe contracts.

title: Audit FrankenSim for bounded reuse without coupling the demo runtime
description:
## Outcome
Evaluate Jeffrey Emanuel's FrankenSim at a pinned commit as a possible source of reusable deterministic numerics, SDF/voxel/meshing, or offline terrain tooling. Do not make it a demo-runtime dependency by enthusiasm alone.

## Current evidence
Upstream describes FrankenSim as a Rust source workspace/library substrate with no packaged end-user simulator or crates.io release, zero registered L3 integrated workflows, and physics emphasis on certified geometry/numerics, meshing, FEM, conduction and airflow rather than a ready real-time game collision API.

## Four-hour stop/go audit
Record commit, license, build/toolchain and dependency constellation; real-time sweep/collision API; dynamic heightfield/SDF mutation; stable serialization/replay; C ABI or Unity/Web/IL2CPP integration path; Linux headless and browser support; deterministic platform claim; maintenance/integration burden.

## Conditional spike
Only if the audit finds a credible narrow API, allow at most three days for a carpet controller, 500 swept projectiles, 200 actors, 32 terrain edits and 10,000-tick save/replay on Linux headless plus Web target.

## Acceptance criteria
- Stop after the audit if any load-bearing runtime need lacks an implemented supported path.
- Adopt only if replay hashes repeat, authoritative tick cost stays below 2 ms at demo load, allocations remain bounded, terrain updates are usable, and the option yields at least 30% less integration code or 2x measured performance versus the pure C# baseline.
- Otherwise retain custom quantized fixed-tick C# simulation and consider FrankenSim only for isolated offline tooling/research.
- No FFI enters the critical path without a separate approved architecture change.

title: Pin the Blender 4.5 LTS patch and toolchain checksums
description:
## Outcome
Pin the exact Blender 4.5 LTS patch and reproducible toolchain identity used by every asset-authoring, CI, and import lane without installing or changing the machine in this bead.

## Inputs
- Official Blender release and checksum/signature sources.
- Accepted asset-pipeline, provenance, CI, and standard-installation policies.
- Target Linux workstation and future CI platform matrix.

## Owned output
A versioned pin record containing the Blender version/build identity, official archive or installer URL, SHA-256, upstream checksum or signature evidence, supported host targets, headless version probe, and consumers.

## Non-goals
- Do not install Blender, enable extensions, choose an MCP, author an asset, or create project-local wrappers.
- Do not use experimental/nightly builds or unverified mirrors.
- Do not unpack system tools into the repository or an unusual prefix to avoid legitimate sudo.

## Procedure
1. Resolve the latest approved 4.5 LTS patch from official Blender sources.
2. Record platform-specific release artifact identity and cryptographic evidence.
3. Define the standard system or tool-owned installation path for each host.
4. Specify the exact headless probe and expected normalized output.
5. Define how CI, Blender automation, asset manifests, and Unity import evidence consume the pin.
6. Record upgrade, rollback, cache invalidation, and incompatible-file handling.

## Acceptance criteria
- The pin names exact semantic version, build hash/date where exposed, platform/architecture, official source URL, SHA-256, and upstream verification evidence.
- A documented command verifies the downloaded artifact before installation and a separate command reports the running headless version/build.
- The pin is machine-readable and referenced by planned CI, MCP bakeoff, bpy recipe, asset-manifest, and Unity-import lanes.
- Upgrade and rollback rules prevent silently opening/resaving production blend files with an unapproved version.
- Offline/cache behavior and failure messages are defined.
- No installation occurs without a separately authorized bead; this bead may close on the reproducible pin artifact alone.
- Failure evidence records source URL, HTTP status, observed checksum/signature, expected value, platform, command, stderr, and timestamp.

title: [L2] Complete remc2 -> Rust -> Unity Level 2 without new per-level authority
description:
## Mission

Complete owner Level 2 through deterministic Rust simulation, the existing campaign C ABI, and Unity presentation while leaving no new Level-2-only authority that the next realm must replace.

This is the program closure parent. Do not claim it for implementation. Claim one ready capability leaf.

## Architecture outcome

- Level 1 remains sealed. Level 2 lands monotonically on the current production route; broad campaign folding waits for revision-bound Level 2 evidence.
- Rust is the sole gameplay authority. Unity consumes the generic campaign ABI and owner-data presentation mapping.
- New behavior is keyed by its exact source dispatch site/class/action and required model/subtype context, not by a friendly family name alone.
- Slot identity, allocation/reclaim order, source schedule, RNG, terrain, objectives, reset/hash composition, and ordered effects retain one canonical authority each. Families are delivery groupings, not new authorities; the C ABI and Unity are projections, not simulation owners.
- “Shared engine” does not mean a generic dictionary, ECS, plugin registry, trait-object hot path, scripting DSL, or one universal enemy struct.

## Accretive rule

Every child must deliver a positive Level 2 production behavior without adding another writable mirror, per-level RNG, Level-N session/API, Unity gameplay rule, or approximation that a later realm must replace. Reuse exact existing carriers and generic consumers. Existing Level 1 behavior stays green and is not mined for abstractions before a post-Level-2 equivalence experiment proves the seam.

## Required vertical capability families

1. campaign content selection, authored package, terrain/flight, activation and source schedule;
2. creatures: Goat, Bee, class-5 model-3, class-5 model-9, Archer construction, Trader/model-14, civilians and other rooted families;
3. Nyphur/wizard AI, combat, casting, death, respawn and banishment;
4. spells/effects, holders, projectiles and terrain effects;
5. mana/economy, pickups, buildings/castles and destruction;
6. objectives, terminal result, RNG/audio ordering and deterministic replay;
7. generic C ABI snapshots/events and Unity terrain, entities, effects, HUD, minimap, localization, audio/music and ordinary input;
8. one final, non-empty Level 2 play route and qualification pass.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every reachable Level 2 denominator is implemented exactly or excluded mechanically against remc2 `6806c7204d17220ecc0430759f784aea8ee2ddb2` plus qualified owner data.
- [ ] No new Level-2-specific mutable authority, session/API family, or Unity gameplay implementation was added; any common-behavior claim retains dispatch-site/RNG/schedule context until equivalence is proven.
- [ ] Level 1 preserves accepted ordering, arithmetic, RNG, reset, hashes, ABI behavior and focused controls.
- [ ] Level 2 runs from ordinary Unity input through Rust, the generic campaign ABI and owner-data presentation to terminal mission result.
- [ ] Reset/replay reproduces generation, state, ordered events/audio and hashes; unknown package/profile/source identities fail closed.
- [ ] No `Level3ResetSession`, level-numbered ABI family, Unity gameplay authority, placeholder, mock-only positive path, test-only production mutation, or regenerated golden used to accept changed behavior exists.
- [ ] The accepted Level 2 candidate unblocks the bounded campaign-fold/Level 3 delta-planning Bead; no second matrix, dashboard, readiness ledger or architecture ceremony is required.

## No-claim

Level 2 closure does not establish later realms, cross-level handler equivalence, the post-Level-2 authority fold, or permission for Track P implementation to cross into Track S. It establishes only the accepted Levels 1-2 routes and the observations exercised by them.

title: Define reversible prototype distribution and licensing guardrails
description:
## What
Define reversible prototype distribution, licensing, compatibility, and publication guardrails while deliberately deferring the long-term business model until feasibility evidence exists.

## Recorded decision
Oliver will decide commercial premium, free, donation-supported, open source, or another release model after the feasibility slice has demonstrated fun, technical cost, content throughput, and hosting burden.

## Pre-prototype decisions still required
Private versus publicly visible development; ownership and contributor terms; dependencies/assets we may legally replace or redistribute; whether source can be published before a permanent license is chosen; trademark/branding boundaries; treatment of generated or outsourced work; and whether user-owned-data compatibility remains deferred.

## Acceptance criteria
- Prototype code and artifacts can be developed without creating an accidental public license, service promise, or irreversible dependency.
- Any publicly visible checkout is publication-safe and has an explicit temporary or permanent license posture; absent that, it remains private.
- Code, original assets, third-party assets, fonts, audio, shaders, server, and tools have allowed prototype license classes and replacement rules.
- Compatibility/importer work is forbidden or deferred behind separate legal review during feasibility.
- Contributor IP policy is defined before accepting contributions.
- Hosting remains disposable and incurs no continuity promise.
- A post-feasibility decision bead uses measured evidence to choose the actual release/business/source-license model.

title: Build the finite-mana economy, pacing, and stalemate simulation
description:
## Outcome
Prove the proposed demo economy and faction rules in a fast headless model before expensive content implementation.

## Model
Track one conserved ledger across neutral, wizard/faction-owned exposed, carrier-reserved, in-transit, stronghold-secured, player/actor-held, structure-held, spent-and-transformed, and legitimately re-released states. No hidden resource creation, duplication, or deletion is allowed without an explicit sink/source rule.

## Scenarios
Run deterministic seeded solo, co-op, FFA, fixed 2v2, and mixed human/AI scenarios across harvest, raid, rush, defense, carrier-intercept, and terrain-control policies. Test 55%, 60%, and 65% thresholds, stronghold placements, route lengths, carrier loss, player death, emergency rebuild, inaccessible mana, volcano phases, timeout, exit hold, and overtime cache.

## Metrics
Time to first kill, claim, stronghold, delivery, upgrade, rival contact, leader change, threshold, exit and completion; carrier throughput/loss; exposed versus secured mana; comeback frequency; elimination and idle time; inaccessible/unrecoverable mana; cleanup fraction; timeout and stalemate frequency; strategy win share.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every run reconciles the ledger exactly.
- No policy wins more than 65% across at least 50 balanced seeded bot trials.
- Reverse-circle strafing is not universally safe and stronghold construction is not the dominant attack.
- Typical completion is 20-30 minutes; no player lacks a visible productive action for more than 90 seconds; cleanup is under 25% of run time.
- At least two strategic approaches remain viable.
- Threshold, carrier, recovery, overtime and comeback parameters are exported as versioned tuning data with rationale.
- Failures produce seed, policy, timeline, ledger trace and first invariant violation.

title: [L2] Bind player Castle cast to mana/upkeep carrier
description:
## Deliverable
Bind the qualified Level 2 player's authored Castle holder to the real requested-spell command route, source-shaped human Castle projectile/construction dispatcher, exact evolving Castle relation, and overlap-gated player upkeep. This is the first missing production carrier for ordinary Invisible and Beyond Sight reachability; it is not Castle teardown work and does not falsely claim to create Castle mana.

## Authority and ownership
- Pinned read-only specification: remc2 `6806c7204d17220ecc0430759f784aea8ee2ddb2`.
- Exact human-route anchors: requested-spell input and `sub_5F660` (`EventsFunctions.cpp:60892-60924`), model-2 holder activation, Castle projectile constructor `sub_4D900` (class 9/model 10), `CastCastleProjectile_66B30`, `EndOfCastleProjectile_5F8F0`, `BeginOfCastleCreation_5FA70`, `sub_60480`, player upkeep `AddPlayer03_00_5E010`, and overlap `sub_106C0`.
- The writes at `EventsFunctions.cpp:6837` and `:43832` are AI-only paths. They are not evidence for the ordinary human command route.
- Reuse accepted Castle state/controller/arena and the existing player upkeep function. Do not create a second Castle, spell, mana, input, relation, or upkeep authority.
- Read but never edit `upstream/magic-carpet-2-hd/`.

## Exact production route
Qualified Level 2 package -> authored local family-2 holder from `mc-bvihb.6` -> `McCampaignStepInputV2.command.requested_spell` as the UI index mapping through `SOURCE_SPELL_INDEX_MAP` to family 2, with cast flag `0x40` -> existing `sub_5F660`-shaped activation -> class-9/model-10 human Castle projectile -> `CastCastleProjectile_66B30` collision allocation of a distinct class-3/model-2 Castle seed -> `BeginOfCastleCreation_5FA70` -> successful child/site creation -> `sub_60480` writes the player Castle relation to the class-3/model-2 root at construction start. The human route does not write the relation to the flying projectile or before successful `sub_60480`.

## Acceptance criteria
- A qualified ordinary Level 2 C ABI/Unity command, not a helper/setter, selects the UI slot mapping to family 2 and activates the existing holder. `requested_spell` is not assumed equal to family; no new opcode.
- Missing/inactive holder, no cast flag, invalid selection, occupied Castle relation, class-9 projectile allocation failure, collision/root allocation failure, and site/child failure follow source behavior without slot/relation leaks. Occupied relation may run holder activation but spawns no second Castle route.
- Successful activation first allocates the class-9/model-10 human projectile without changing `CastleEntityIndex`. `CastCastleProjectile_66B30` later allocates the distinct class-3/model-2 seed on collision. Only successful `sub_60480` writes `CastleEntityIndex` to that root at construction start; do not delay until action-4 completion and do not borrow the AI-only immediate relation write.
- Site/construction failure preserves the source word/action schedule, writes no Castle relation, and never launders a projectile or seed into a built Castle.
- Extend the one existing player upkeep authority. Preserve order: add prior mana/life regen; clamp; then choose Castle/boost recharge only when the current relation resolves and `sub_106C0` shift-AABB overlap (or source byte1 `0x10`) is true. Use both real player and Castle extents. On overlap set mana regen `max(maxMana/200,1000)`, life regen `maxLife/250`, clear boost bit, and apply `word_0x159=2`; otherwise retain outdoor `max(maxMana/2000,100)` and `maxLife/2000`.
- Public campaign turns prove requested Castle cast, projectile and root allocation order, relation timing, construction progression, on-Castle vs off-Castle recharge, reset/generation/replay/hash, and negative fail-closed behavior. No `build_castle_at`, direct mana write, `Some(2000)`, synthetic state, or AI-only shortcut is credited.
- Castle mana and player mana are distinct. This Bead may prove existing Castle-mana deposit composition if naturally reachable, but it must not claim Invisible/Beyond activation unless both meet the pinned predicate through source-real routes. Otherwise name Castle-mana filling as remaining consumer work.
- Rust implementation, stable C ABI/managed route where required, and discriminating tests land together. Level 1 and remc2 remain untouched.

## Narrow ownership
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-core/src/native_world.rs`
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-core/src/native_world/level2_dynamic_economy.rs` only for existing source allocator/Castle controller reuse or a proven correction
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-capi/src/native_v2.rs` only for a focused stable step/snapshot proof
- Managed files only if a real boundary defect is observed; no speculative Unity change

## Focused verification
- Exact sim-core public-command test: UI selection -> family-2 holder -> class-9 projectile with relation still zero -> collision class-3 root -> successful construction-start relation write -> no premature built event.
- Exact negatives: flags zero, missing holder, occupied relation, projectile allocation failure, root allocation failure, and site/child failure.
- Exact upkeep tests: off-Castle AABB retains outdoor rates; on-Castle overlap and boost use Castle rates after add-then-clamp, including life and `word_0x159` coupling.
- Exact sim-capi test through `mc_native_campaign_session_step`, using nonzero selection.
- Existing outdoor upkeep, Castle controller, reset, and teardown focused tests remain green; fmt, correctness/suspicious Clippy, diff-check, UBS. Run non-empty Unity Level 2 EditMode only if managed changes.

## Process boundary and nonclaims
This Bead exists because one observed missing production carrier blocks two named playable spells. It retires when public requested-spell commands create and advance the human Castle route and player upkeep is source-exact. It does not own Castle teardown (`mc-bvihb.2`), opponent AI, a generalized spell refactor, or unproved Castle-mana generation.

title: [L2] Tier-0 Possession claims model-39 and feeds Castle economy
description:
## Deliverable
Bind the ordinary Level 2 tier-0 Possession cast to the existing model-39 mana-sphere ownership mailbox and Castle economy. Reuse the current public campaign input and arena; add no command, ABI layout, Level-N API, generic projectile framework, or presentation work.

## Exact remc2 lifecycle
Pinned remc2 `6806c7204d17220ecc0430759f784aea8ee2ddb2` is read-only. `UpdateEntities_57730` scans source slots in ascending order, dispatches, increments the entity phase after every callback, and reclaims disabled rows only in the following pass prologue.

- Ordinary holder: Level 2 local holder 116, class15/model1/action3. `sub_69640` validates the holder and on tier-0 life zero calls `sub_69900`, creating class9/model1/action1 with impact output class10/model12. The holder's expenditure/decrement still occurs if projectile allocation fails.
- Projectile: `SummonManaPosession_4D3B0`; runtime `CastPosses_65F60`. It moves, then `sub_108B0` walks map chains deterministically and selects the first eligible strict-overlap target. The bounded positive target is an already materialized class10/model39 mana sphere. Only successful model12 effect allocation copies caster identity and disables the projectile; allocation failure leaves it live and writes nothing.
- Effect: `NewAdd0A0C_4E8C0` creates class10/model12/action12. `PossesHitMana_320E0` -> `sub_112D0` writes target mailbox `word_0x68=effect.id` and payload zero only while the target remains live, mapped, flagged, and in strict overlap. Its life sequence and following-pass reclaim remain source ordered.
- Consumer: model39/action41 `TransformArcherToMana_35940` consumes the mailbox. If the incoming owner differs and the block flag is clear, it writes `playerEntityIndex`, clears the mailbox/payload and ownership flag, and emits the existing sound/economy consequences. Rust must keep its duplicate owner projection synchronized because current economy consumers inspect both.

Fireball is explicitly not this producer: its separate holder/projectile damages but never writes ownership. The current authored class10/model22 Wind row is not the source class5/model22 death-to-sphere route and must remain untargetable here.

## Ownership
One writer owns only:

- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-core/src/native_world.rs`
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-core/src/native_world/level2_dynamic_economy.rs`
- `research/private/remc2-sim-rs/crates/sim-capi/src/native_v2.rs` for focused public-route tests only; no ABI/layout change.

Add typed tier-0 class9/model1/action1 projectile and class10/model12/action12 effect variants to the existing dynamic arena, including stable appended family codes, enumeration, dispatch, reset/replay/hash, free-list, capacity and reclaim. Higher-slot allocations may dispatch later in the current pass; lower-slot allocations wait until the next pass.

## Ordinary positive route
Through `mc_native_campaign_session_step` only:

1. Move the player with ordinary `McCampaignStepInputV2` coordinates onto the authored group-1 switch so the existing producer materializes real class10/model39 spheres.
2. Issue the existing cast input `flags=0x40`, `requested_spell=1`.
3. Observe holder116 produce class9/model1/action1; advance ordinary steps until it selects the first qualifying model39 row and produces class10/model12/action12.
4. Prove collision alone does not change ownership; the effect callback writes the mailbox and the model39/action41 callback performs and clears the ownership change.
5. Use the existing ordinary Castle `requested_spell=2` route and advance until the existing defender/carrier collection consumes the newly owned sphere and changes Castle mana.
6. Assert projectile/effect same-pass phase and following-pass reclaim.

No direct allocation, mailbox mutation, position setter, sphere-claim helper, Castle spawn/mana setter, Level 1 house-possession bridge, or event injection may stand in for this route.

## Discriminating negatives
- Fireball cannot change ownership.
- Authored class10/model22 Wind; wrong class/model; blocked model45; self ID; already-owned target; and equality on any strict-overlap boundary do not hit.
- Model12 allocation exhaustion leaves the projectile active and writes no mailbox. Projectile allocation exhaustion still applies source holder expenditure/decrement.
- Collision without the effect callback cannot change ownership. The mailbox is consumed and cleared; repeated effect pulses do not double-claim or double-credit.
- Lower-slot allocation does not dispatch in the allocating pass; higher-slot allocation may. Reset restores arena/free-list/mailboxes/RNG/hash and two sessions remain isolated.

## Focused verification
Ship exact core production/lifecycle, predicates/order/failure, public C-ABI route, and reset/isolation tests. Suggested names are `level_two_public_possession_claims_model39_and_feeds_castle_economy`, `level_two_possession_preserves_target_slot_and_allocation_failure_semantics`, `level2_campaign_requested_possession_claims_model39_through_public_step`, and `level2_campaign_possession_reset_replay_is_exact_and_isolated`. Discover each exact test first and reject a zero-test result. Run format, focused sim-core and sim-capi correctness/suspicious Clippy, `python3 tools/verify_level2_profile.py --json`, and the locked workspace lane before integration.

## No-claims
This does not implement advanced Possession tiers, class5/model22 production/death conversion, Fireball fidelity, Unity presentation, a new ABI, direct player mana reaching 2400, Castle mana reaching 10000, or closure of Invisible/Beyond Sight. It supplies the missing ordinary ownership producer and a real downstream economy consumer; the spell closures retain their remaining source-backed mana/capacity prerequisites.

description:

- Validation builds a candidate and complete bounded diagnostics without publication.
- Apply atomically exposes definition pointer/revision, package/artifact graph, active bindings and durable receipt at one commit point and verifies read-back hash.
- Identical idempotent retry returns the original receipt; rollback is a new guarded revision to an explicitly retained content graph.
- CLI supports inspect -> bounded describe -> preview -> guarded apply with versioned data-only stdout, diagnostics on stderr, bounded pagination and typed remediation.

## Discriminating negatives

Stale expected definition, key reuse with different bytes, invalid cross-field dependency, partial asset graph, fault before/after every durable boundary and cancel-before-commit preserve every authoritative root. This publishes immutable definitions but does not mutate or rebind live sessions and does not prove gameplay uses any writable value. On failure, remove only the active candidate pointer/change and retain content-addressed artifacts/receipts for diagnosis; the last accepted definition and sealed Level 1 route remain authoritative.

title: Build the native Unity flight harness over the exact Rust simulation core
description:
## Outcome
Produce an owner-local Linux desktop Unity flight harness that feels like MC2 because every authoritative flight tick is executed by the reconciled Rust sim-core, not rewritten in C# or Unity physics.

## Architecture
Add a narrow versioned C ABI adapter around sim-core, build a normal x86_64 Linux shared library, and consume it from a Unity 6000.3.20f1 desktop project. Unity owns relative mouse/keyboard input, camera, presentation, audio and HUD only. Rust owns command latching, scheduler, movement, terrain collision, tether and spell activation state. Start with one deterministic owner-local terrain/profile fixture; do not modify pinned remc2.

## Acceptance
1. Fullscreen and windowed Linux players launch from reproducible CLI commands and capture the mouse reliably; escape releases capture and quitting is explicit.
2. The Unity player calls the Rust adapter every fixed simulation tick and displays returned state/hash; no flight equation is duplicated in C# or Rigidbody/PhysX.
3. W/S, strafe, yaw, pitch and fire input work; a visible fireball proves the fire event boundary without making presentation authoritative.
4. A headless scripted command replay through the adapter matches the sim-core golden hash/state, and Unity EditMode/PlayMode smoke tests cover ABI layout and input-to-command translation.
5. Camera near plane, terrain collision and spawn configuration eliminate the clipping that obscured the browser proof.
6. Build/run/test commands, plugin copy step, versions and known presentation-only differences are documented. Track P data and identifiers remain owner-local.
notes: First playable native milestone is built. Added sim-capi scalar ABI over exact sim-core and owner level-1 state/terrain; no flight equations in C# or PhysX. Unity 6000.3.20f1 Linux player builds reproducibly and packages libsim_capi.so. Packaged headless self-test PASS: hash 956246bd7f270164, position 19840,56480,5040, phase 161 after eight forward ticks. Full Rust gate PASS at 98 tests (87 sim-core, 4 atlas, 3 sim-capi, 4 parked wasm), strict fmt/clippy, atlas 24/24 and 14,496/14,496. 2026-07-24 correction pass: traced ComputeMousePlayerMovement_17060 and replaced one-tick mouse impulses with a persistent absolute [-127,127] virtual cursor; C/MMB explicitly recentres. I/J/K/L use the same source command so real virtual-device playtesting is repeatable. Held/released steering screenshots prove command 83 persisted while yaw advanced 698 to 1458. Rebuilt terrain as all 256x256 source cells at 256-unit spacing, retained world-edge vertex coordinates while wrapping only samples, and matched alternating source diagonals; removed non-source placeholder landmarks. Camera now uses display_pitch rather than terrain-shaped effective_pitch. Deterministic graphical self-play covers acceleration, both steering directions, pitch, strafe and two fires, captures five checkpoints, and PASSes at tick 440 (turn true, altitude true, fire 2). Final packaged self-test retains the golden hash and all 98 Rust tests pass. Remaining before bead closure: Unity EditMode/PlayMode smoke tests and user feel feedback/polish.
close_reason: Acceptance is now proven by the qualified Rust-owned Unity desktop path: versioned C ABI, input/fire routing, headless replay, EditMode 31/31, PlayMode 1/1, fixed presentation profile, and current documentation.

title: Gate exact remc2 presentation or one controlled Unity modernization deviation
description: Purpose: prevent source-presentation work from either drifting indefinitely or being abandoned casually. Exact remc2 Level 1 presentation remains the default target. title: Repair remc2-faithful Possession, spell menu, and Speed presentation
description:
## Human symptom

Owner playthrough 20260727T115617.7801260Z-pid3134758 showed Possession projectiles hitting buildings but rendering as Fireball explosions, no persistent blue possessed-building marker, a misleading bottom-centre Fireball icon, and no discoverable faithful spell switching. Oliver asked that fixes follow remc2 rather than local improvisation.

## Confirmed remc2 contracts

- Tier-zero Possession uses class9/model1 and creates class10/model12/action12 at the target top. Model12 uses render parameter 41, fixed base TMAP54, life8.
- Model12 calls sub_112D0(entity,0) during each live update, writing caster ownership into nearby target mailboxes. AddHouse0A_2D_38330 consumes the mailbox, changes persistent owner, switches render parameter to177/TMAP96 with player-colour offset, then clears the mailbox.
- A successful target hit calls sub_6D8B0(player, Possession family1, +1), then the single-player sub_6D9C0 tier recomputation.
- MouseAndKeysEvents_17A00 and DrawBottomSpellsMenu_2ECC0 use held Control for the 2x13 spell menu and independent equipped hands. LMB/RMB select and assign the family/tier to left/right using actions31/32. Normal LMB/RMB cast those hands.
- Speed Up itself sets 240 initial speed, 160 sustain and 80 restore, emits sound19 and a class10/model2 trail. Manual speed input cancels it. Palette submode3 green tint belongs to the moveSpeed slowing/impairment state, not Speed Up. Generic speed blur begins above baseline speed according to display settings.

## Root causes

- terrain_frame.rs routes every non-splash impact through Fireball render index7/base38, so the model12 marker appears as a Fireball explosion.
- Rust models neither the model12 possession mailbox nor persistent building owner/render change, and omits successful-use XP/tier recomputation.
- Unity always draws an invented selected spell at 288,432 and uses invented 1-4 plus Q controls instead of the source Control menu and two-hand assignment flow.
- Rust incorrectly applies palette submode3 while Speed Up is active.

## Acceptance

1. Model12 impact renders through parameter41, fixed TMAP54 and logical height250, never Fireball 38+phase; exact world-frame tests distinguish it.
2. Its live area-effect writes the source-equivalent possession mailbox; Level1 buildings consume it in source order, persist owner state, switch to render parameter177/TMAP96/player colour and emit source sound4. Recorder exposes ownership.
3. Each successful owned-player building hit adds exactly one Possession XP and recomputes source tier thresholds from qualified spell data; misses and terrain do not.
4. Hold Control exposes a source-shaped 2x13 owner-asset spell menu. Only enabled families are assignable. LMB assigns left and RMB assigns right with opcode31/32 semantics; release returns to flight; normal LMB/RMB cast the equipped hands.
5. Remove the invented bottom-centre selected-spell icon/outline and Q/number-key primary path from qualified human play. Any debug shortcut is off by default.
6. Remove the false Speed-Up green palette coupling. Preserve exact speed impulse/sustain/restore/cancel and add source sound/trail; implement or visibly defer source-configured high-speed blur without claiming it.
7. Recorder adds hand/menu, Possession XP/tier/building owner and speed/effect state sufficient to prove future runs.
8. Focused Rust tests, Unity EditMode/PlayMode tests, desktop build and recorded self-test pass. No DOSBox or original executable is used.

Final reviewer APPROVE after correcting opcode6 so flags-zero movement preserves spell selection and only flags&0x40 changes it. title: [GFX] Epic: private Exact, Classic HD, and Unity Enhanced presentation modes
description:
## Player outcome
Ship three mutually exclusive owner-local presentation modes over the same remc2/owned-data -> Rust simulation -> Unity game. This program modernizes presentation without changing gameplay, object identity, or the preservation boundary.

## Non-negotiable mode contract
1. Exact Preservation remains sealed: the qualified 320x200 indexed frame, corrected 4:3 display, owner HUD, hashes, project, and corpus do not receive modern effects or content changes.
2. Classic HD is remc2-style HD: rerender the same indexed terrain, sprites, palette behavior, source order, and owner HUD at a higher internal resolution. Internal render size is separate from window size. Scaling, filtering, buffer sizes, projection, and HUD composition may improve; object art and HUD identity may not be replaced.
3. Unity Enhanced is the same owner game in 3D space. It may use source-derived terrain tessellation, source-derived normals and material response, dynamic lights and shadows, night fog, real scene reflections, event-driven ripples, bloom, motion effects, AA, render scaling, and upscaling. It may not replace a house, castle, creature, pickup, terrain feature, or HUD element with authored, imported, AI-generated, generic, or procedural substitute art.

## Visual provenance rule
Classify every accepted owner-route visual as exactly one of:
- OwnerIdentity: qualified owner indexed sprite, palette, animation, facing, visibility, source order, or owner HUD data.
- SourceDerivedSurface: rendering geometry derived only from authoritative heightfield, terrain type, shoreline, BUILD footprint, or other Rust/remc2 source state. Resampling and tessellation are allowed; invented roofs, windows, silhouettes, and landmarks are not.
- AuthoritativeEffect: transient renderer geometry or post-processing anchored to a real generation/tick-bound Rust entity or event, such as Fireball trail/light/shimmer/impact, smoke, spell light, water ripple, reflection, fog, or speed streak. It may beautify the event but may not become substitute gameplay-object identity.
- DiagnosticOnly: boxes, generic meshes, synthetic entities, and fixtures behind an explicit non-owner diagnostic flag. DiagnosticOnly visuals are forbidden in accepted owner captures.

Unknown, unqualified, or missing OwnerIdentity visuals fail closed and remain an explicit coverage exclusion; they never fall back to Generic. The test is recognition: if changing a visual changes what the player recognizes the object as, it is identity and must be owner/source-derived.

## Implementation base and writer rule
As of 2026-08-04, canonical main ccd8419 does not contain the Enhanced stack. The clean implementation baseline is commit f088f2c5da051f4f217ddba60e3b51e73cf9d248 on codex/gfx-spec. The live worktree /home/oliver/ntm_Dev/magiccarpet-gfx-spec is dirty and must not be used by another writer. Each worker creates or receives one isolated clean worktree from the exact integration commit named by GFX-T, records that base in its first bead comment, and touches only its assigned files. Candidate sibling commits are advisory inputs; inspect and port the semantic delta instead of blind cherry-picking. One writer owns each checkout.

## Architecture and boundaries
Rust remains authoritative for simulation, terrain edits, entities, spells, objectives, RNG, events, saves, and replay hashes. Renderer choices may not alter command, event, gameplay-state, checkpoint, or save results. The Exact project and corpus remain immutable. VoxelMode is separate and cannot supply structures or art. Owner data stays external and private; no private payload enters a build or Track S.

## Release acceptance
Level 1 Night must run through the same honest command stream in all modes. Exact remains byte-identical. Classic HD has one frozen supported-resolution matrix and authentic HiDPI owner HUD. Unity Enhanced must visibly remain the same game in fresh opaque owner captures: recognizable source terrain/buildings/actors/HUD, with modern lighting and effects on top. Required review routes are town approach/overflight, ordinary fight, Fireball cast/flight/impact, water/reflection/real ripple, normal/high-speed flight, death/restart, and completion where the authoritative journal supports it. Fixture tests, retained images, llvmpipe/software captures, alpha-broken PNGs, or receipts marked not-reviewed are not visual acceptance.

## Guardrails
Track P private only. Do not use DOSBox, the original executable, decompilers, or original-binary oracle work. Do not move owner assets into Unity or a player build. Use focused tests during slices and one full Exact Unity gate only at the final integration milestone. Do not create process artifacts unless they enforce a named feature or hard release gate.

title: [GFX-O] Qualify Classic HD Level 1 and publish the supported-resolution matrix
description:
## Outcome
Qualify Classic HD as the authentic remc2-style high-resolution form of the existing game, not as an asset remake. Freeze one reproducible supported-resolution matrix and stop re-running unchanged decisions.

## Required behavior
Classic HD rerenders the same indexed terrain, palette behavior, source-ordered sprites, reflections, blur/history, minimap, cursor, and owner HUD at a larger internal buffer. It may change projection/buffer dimensions, scaling, filtering, and window composition. It may not replace source assets, terrain identity, sprite identity, or HUD identity. Optional high-resolution owner banks remain a separately hash-gated future tier and are not required for this release.

## Execution
1. Use the clean designated Classic HD integration commit; do not write in a dirty shared worktree.
2. Reproduce the latest owner-route performance trace once for any code delta that can change it. Do not re-run the same trace without a named uncertainty.
3. Freeze the current T14 decision unless relevant code or hardware changes: 640x480 is supported when p95 total frame generation/copy is at or below 33.333 ms with no recurring steady bulk allocation; 960x720 and 1280x960 remain visible as measured unsupported profiles unless fresh evidence on the exact candidate commit proves otherwise.
4. Run honest owner Level 1 idle, town, combat, normal/high-speed flight, death/restart, fullscreen/window, alt-tab, fallback, and the available completion/postgame journal path. Bind receipts to exact commit, owner manifest, settings, and hardware.
5. Verify the owner HUD/minimap/cursor are the actual source presentation at the selected internal resolution and corrected 4:3 output, not a Unity replacement.
6. Run the nearest Rust/C ABI/Unity tests and matrix validator. Run the full Exact gate only once at the final package milestone.

## Acceptance criteria
- 640x480 has a fresh exact-build owner-route PASS under the 30 Hz CPU/copy budget, zero recurring steady bulk allocation, no dropped/out-of-order frames, and deterministic indexed checkpoints.
- 960x720 and 1280x960 are explicitly PASS or REJECT with bound evidence. A rejected profile is not marketed as supported.
- Window resolution and internal render resolution are independently selectable and accurately reported.
- Town, combat, flight, death/restart, owner HUD, minimap, cursor, reflections, lighting, and blur/history are visibly the same indexed game at higher resolution.
- Exact fast guards pass after relevant changes, cross-mode gameplay hashes agree, owner data remains external, and the final matrix validator passes.
- T14 reports unsupported GPU timing/fence honestly. Lack of an async GPU fence on this hardware does not block the CPU/copy-supported matrix and is not represented as captured GPU proof.
- Automatic Speed-jar postprocess is deferred until the authoritative owner ABI exposes a legitimate activation route. It does not block Level 1 Classic HD qualification; fixture-only activation may test rendering but is not gameplay proof.
- No placeholder corpus, not-reviewed capture, or repeated unchanged receipt is used as closure evidence.

## Guardrails
Track P private only. Exact project/corpus remain immutable. Rust remains gameplay authority. Do not use DOSBox, the original executable, decompilers, or original-binary oracle work. Do not embed owner data, use new art, use VoxelMode, or weaken a budget/golden/assertion to pass.

title: [GFX-Z] Qualify, package, and accept the three-mode private presentation release
description:
## Outcome
Package and accept the three owner-local modes as a reproducible player experience: sealed Exact, authentic remc2-style Classic HD, and the same owner game rendered beautifully in Unity Enhanced.

## Integration base
The Enhanced implementation currently lives on codex/gfx-spec rather than canonical main. Final qualification runs only after GFX-T integrates the corrected owner-visual stack onto one clean candidate commit and that candidate is available through the normal project integration path. Branch-only code, dirty-worktree output, or evidence from a different commit cannot close this bead.

## Work
1. Build the Exact Built-in player and the URP presentation-lab player; expose Exact, ClassicHD, and UnityEnhanced through documented pre-session selection.
2. Run identical honest Level 1 Night command streams for idle, town, combat, Fireball cast/flight/impact, water interaction, normal/high-speed flight, death/restart, available completion, and postgame.
3. Compare command, event, gameplay-state, checkpoint/save, and available replay hashes. Validate renderer exclusivity, reset/teardown, input, audio, owner HUD, minimap, supported settings, privacy, build payload, and error recovery.
4. Use the GFX-O frozen Classic HD matrix. Do not reopen 960x720 or GPU-fence decisions unless the exact candidate code or target hardware changed.
5. Re-verify GFX-U through GFX-X on the corrected owner-identity substrate. Preserve legal lighting, shadows, fog, Fireball shimmer/light/impact, water reflection/real ripple, post, AA, render scaling, and upscaling. Fix only concrete regressions.
6. Run focused Rust/C ABI/Unity gates and one final full Exact Unity qualification gate. Produce one fresh acceptance corpus and one reviewer verdict instead of repeated not-reviewed captures.

## Acceptance criteria
- Exact artifacts are byte-identical to GFX-A and its project/corpus remain untouched.
- Classic HD satisfies GFX-O: same indexed game and authentic source HUD at supported resolution; unsupported profiles remain explicit.
- GFX-T is closed. Every Enhanced identity-bearing visual is OwnerIdentity or SourceDerivedSurface; unknowns fail closed. DiagnosticOnly boxes, generated chalets/castles/creatures/pickups, generic fallbacks, and replacement HUD panels are absent from the accepted owner profile.
- Enhanced fresh owner captures visibly read as the original Level 1 Night game: same terrain/building/actor/HUD identity, improved by modern renderer technology.
- Town approach/overflight shows source-derived settlement/terrain with no chalet overlays. Fight and Fireball frames show the authoritative projectile/event with warm moving light, shimmer/trail, bloom and impact spill. Water frames show real scene reflection and a ripple from an authoritative WaterSplashed event. Flight frames retain readable terrain/HUD at normal and high speed.
- All acceptance PNGs are opaque, captured in a fresh process on a real GPU with external owner inputs, and bound to exact commit/build/settings/owner-manifest hashes. Software/llvmpipe, fixture-only, retained/stale, alpha-broken, transparent, or visual_review_status=not-reviewed frames do not qualify.
- A named human reviewer records pass/fail for town, fight, Fireball, water, flight, and HUD. Any failed route keeps this bead open and names the concrete visual defect.
- The three modes consume the same honest commands and produce identical authoritative simulation outcomes. No mode silently falls into another renderer.
- Builds contain no owner payload and remain private. No new object/HUD art, VoxelMode content, or Track S content is included.
- Documentation explains installation, mode selection, settings, supported/unsupported resolutions, owner-data setup, fallbacks, limitations, and that Classic/Enhanced are presentation modes rather than Exact qualification.

## Deferred, not release blockers
HDRP, expanded widescreen Classic, optional high-resolution owner banks, new assets, VoxelMode, later levels, unsupported T14 async GPU fence timing, and automatic Speed-jar postprocess without an authoritative ABI route remain separately gated. Do not mislabel them as completed or repeatedly rerun them as current acceptance blockers.

## Guardrails
Track P private only. Do not use DOSBox, the original executable, decompilers, or original-binary oracle work. Rust remains gameplay authority. Do not hard-code demo subjects, inject fake state, weaken gates, promote fixture evidence, or rerun the full 75-90+ minute Exact gate more than once for the final candidate.

title: [GFX-T1] Enforce owner-visual provenance and fail closed
description:
## Outcome
Make visual provenance an executable owner-route rule. Every Unity Enhanced visual is classified as OwnerIdentity, SourceDerivedSurface, AuthoritativeEffect, or DiagnosticOnly. Identity visuals select qualified owner/source data or fail closed; they never reach Generic or a generated mesh. Legal transient effects and source-derived terrain remain available.

## Start here

- research/private/remc2-presentation/enhanced-coverage-matrix.json
- existing owner-actor and lifecycle EditMode tests
## Mission boundary
This is private Track P preservation work on the remc2/owned-data -> Rust -> Unity path. Exact remains sealed. Unity Enhanced must be the same owner game with renderer beauty on top, not replacement art. Rust remains gameplay authority; owner data stays external. Do not use DOSBox, the original executable, decompilers, VoxelMode, Track S content, new/imported/AI-generated object art, fake gameplay state, or hard-coded showcase coordinates.

## Clean-base and writer contract

## Implementation recipe
1. Add one explicit provenance/route classification used by the real owner entity path. Do not rely on mesh names or a documentation-only matrix.
2. Classify houses/castles and other source structures as SourceDerivedSurface and keep them out of the actor generated-mesh path.
3. Classify player, creatures, world objects, pickups, and HUD identity as OwnerIdentity. A missing cache, missing selector, unqualified view, invalid generation/tick, or unknown family disables the renderer and emits a specific bounded diagnostic.
4. Classify generation/tick-bound spell, impact, smoke, light, trail, reflection, ripple, fog, and post work as AuthoritativeEffect. Procedural effect geometry remains allowed only while anchored to the authoritative source entity/event and lifetime.
5. Put every generic/box/generated identity fixture behind an explicit non-owner DiagnosticOnly setting that the owner launcher/capture route cannot select. Existing diagnostic tests may opt in.
6. Update the coverage matrix and verifiers to report provenance and fail-closed state. Do not mark an exclusion rendered.
7. Remove the owner-path call chain from unknown/identity rows to GetMesh/CreateMesh/Generic while preserving effect pools and source terrain.

## Pre-stated discriminating tests
- An active class-10/model-45 house row with a source-suppressed or unqualified view does not create a Town/chalet actor renderer.
- An unknown OwnerIdentity selector leaves its renderer disabled with no shared mesh/material and a specific diagnostic; a naive Generic fallback fails this test.
- An explicit DiagnosticOnly fixture can still request a generated box, but the same row under the owner profile cannot.
- A real Fireball/impact event still creates AuthoritativeEffect presentation and remains generation/tick-bound.
- Changing Unity provenance/visibility cannot change Rust command/event/state/checkpoint hashes.

## Acceptance criteria
The focused tests above pass and select nonzero test counts. Static verification finds no owner-route Generic fallback. A fresh owner-source smoke reaches the Enhanced scene without generated identity visuals; exclusions are explicit rather than invisible success. Exact and Classic HD fast guards remain unchanged. Record exact commands, test names, commit, base, and any intentionally retained diagnostic-only functions.

title: [L2-36B1] Expose generation-bound Day indexed frame through campaign C ABI
description:
## Deliverable
Expose the already-qualified Rust Level 2 Day indexed frame through the real campaign handle so Unity can consume frame metadata, indexed bytes, and palette bytes without reimplementing rendering.

This is the missing runtime carrier discovered while executing `mc-exzm.2`. Its concrete consumer is `NativeCampaignSession`/`MagicCarpetRuntime`; it gates the live Level 2 indexed upload/render loop. It retires when the ABI is merged, independently verified, and `mc-exzm.2` can consume it.

## Authority and scope
- Existing renderer: `sim-core/src/day_indexed_frame.rs`, especially `DayIndexedFrameAssets`, `DayIndexedFrameState`, and `render_level2_day_indexed_frame`.
- Existing campaign lifecycle: `sim-capi/src/native_v2.rs`, `sim-capi/include/mc_sim_level2.h`, and Unity `NativeSim.cs`/`NativeCampaignSession.cs` declarations/wrappers.
- Use the current qualified owner Day cache and campaign `inspection`/`reset` state. Do not introduce Unity rendering authority, a Level 1 fallback, captures, generated bytes, or hard-coded frame success.
- Preserve ABI revisioning, reserved-zero fields, generation/tick binding, reset isolation, output-on-failure semantics, bounded bulk copies, hashes, and exact replay.

## Positive observable
An ordinary Level 2 campaign session binds the qualified Day cache, renders the current Rust-authoritative 320x200 indexed frame, returns revisioned metadata, copies exactly 64,000 indices and 768 RGB8 palette bytes, and reproduces identical bytes/hashes after reset/replay at the new generation.

## Planted negatives
- Unknown/tampered cache or non-Level-2 profile fails closed before a frame becomes current.
- Stale generation/tick and pre-render copy fail without returning prior-generation data.
- Undersized/null output buffers report the typed ABI failure and do not claim a complete copy.
- Reset invalidates the old generation and any cached frame.

## Required tests
- Add one exact sim-capi test named `campaign_day_indexed_frame_is_generation_bound_complete_and_fail_closed`; require exactly one selected test and passing positive/negative assertions.
- Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, that exact test with `--locked -- --exact`, focused sim-capi correctness/suspicious Clippy, `git diff --check`, and UBS on changed source.

description:
## Outcome
Validate the exact integrated demo is understandable, enjoyable, strategically expressive, accessible and comfortable.

## Protocol
Use at least ten external players unfamiliar with Magic Carpet, without guide or human coaching, plus a smaller reference-player cohort. Exercise keyboard/mouse, controller, international layouts, low vision, color vision, hearing alternatives, photosensitivity and motion sensitivity. Test solo and the three required social modes.

## Directional gates
- 9/10 deliberately climb, descend, strafe, turn and hit a target within three minutes.
- 8/10 explain why claimed mana has not yet advanced secured victory progress.
- 8/10 secure first mana within five minutes and upgrade a stronghold within ten.
- 7/10 identify two mana sources and one stronghold-site tradeoff.
- 7/10 use deformation when taught and 6/10 later use it spontaneously.
- 7/10 complete in 20-30 minutes.
- No player lacks visible productive action for more than 90 seconds; cleanup is under 25% of run time.
- In a seeded carrier-loss test, 8/10 recover and finish within five added minutes.
- 7/10 choose play another world; 6/10 intend a materially different route.

title: Audit and benchmark pinned Glaurung as an optional local secondary analyzer
description:
## Outcome
Audit exact Glaurung commit db227144364fe0859d44a3a9691b7ee83508ad0d and decide whether it is useful as a local, automation-first secondary analyzer beside Ghidra for the owned DOS-era x86 builds. This is optional and must not block the Ghidra baseline.

## Current warning evidence
The exact revision is Apache-2.0 despite an MIT label in the README comparison table; package version is 0.1.0 and actively evolving. The source tree exposes ELF/PE parsers but no explicit DOS MZ, LE/LX, DOS-extender or overlay loader. Its Python dependencies include pydantic-ai provider clients; configuration auto-discovers parent .env files, reads provider keys, and defaults agent calls to a remote OpenAI model. No owned input may be supplied before this audit passes.

## Audit
- Pin source/archive hash, license/NOTICE, submodules, full Rust/Python dependency locks, build scripts, supported platforms/formats/architectures, project DB migrations, command/tool surface and rollback.
- Trace filesystem/process/network behavior, .env/key discovery, model-provider routing, logs/caches, telemetry, update behavior, patch/source-recovery commands and arbitrary-code surfaces.
- Define an isolated normal install profile with no inherited secrets, network denied, remote LLM tools unavailable, bounded files, reproducible removal and no unusual prefix/PATH workaround.
- Build synthetic known-source x86 fixtures covering DOS MZ, DOS-extender LE/LX where feasible, overlays/relocations, embedded code/data, jump tables, fixed/floating math, PE/ELF controls and intentionally difficult function boundaries.
- Compare Glaurung and pinned Ghidra on loader correctness, disassembly coverage/false code, function boundaries, CFG/xrefs, data references, types, IR/pseudocode semantics, determinism, exportability, memory/time and analyst correction provenance.

## Acceptance
1. Exact source, dependencies, licenses, build/install/remove commands, checksums and re-review trigger are recorded.
2. A no-egress/no-secret profile is proven by source audit plus monitored runtime; no provider key or owned content can leave the lab.
3. Synthetic DOS MZ and MC2-relevant protected-mode/overlay fixtures either load with verified mappings/relocations or produce a clear unsupported decision.
4. Known-source comparison measures semantic/behavioral correctness rather than pretty pseudocode alone and retains minimized failure cases.
5. Glaurung output is classified PRIVATE_ANALYSIS and follows the same transfer gate as Ghidra.
6. Recommendation is accept for named bounded operations, reject, or defer with explicit gaps; unsupported loader/decompiler/debugger behavior cannot be hand-waved.
7. Only after acceptance may a separately scoped campaign feed an owned binary to the pinned local tool.

title: [LEAN-TESTS] Restore a fast, high-signal Level 1/2 development loop
description:
## Outcome
Replace Magic Carpet's blanket, stale, and self-referential gate stack with the smallest test cadence that reliably protects the active remc2 source + owner data -> Rust simulation core -> C ABI -> Unity desktop route. The result must let agents iterate quickly on playable Level 1/2 behavior while retaining direct controls for determinism, owner-data privacy/provenance, ABI integrity, fail-closed package selection, and real Unity reachability.

## Why this exists
The operator explicitly requested this remediation after a read-only HACCP-style audit. Observed defects include: the mandatory Level 2 profile guard fails on a stale sealed-matrix hash; the historical Unity qualifier requires exactly 31 EditMode tests while the assembly now contains 50; all-target Clippy fails with 1,272 mostly pedantic diagnostics; the cached Rust workspace run takes about eight minutes because two soak-scale C-ABI tests dominate it; and seven C-ABI tests expose genuine current Level 2 behavior defects behind the wrapper noise.

## Scope and doctrine
This epic is an implementation program, not a governance program. Leaves must change executable tests, qualification behavior, cache validation, or the commands agents actually run. Do not create a replacement dashboard, matrix, certificate, receipt chain, tracker join, or test-count gate. Do not weaken a behavioral assertion, regenerate a golden to force green, hard-code a demo route, or present a fixture as runtime proof. Long tests may be tiered, split, or parameterized, but the production-capacity/long-route checks remain separately runnable.

Blender CLI/MCP and successor asset production are explicitly out of scope until the clean-room Rust/Unity engine needs agent-authored assets. DOSBox, original-binary oracle work, decompilation, and public/commercial Track S work are also out of scope.

## Program acceptance
- A documented fast development lane exercises touched Rust behavior, relevant C ABI behavior, formatting, focused correctness lints, and the nearest positive runtime path. On a warm 3090 cache, the repository-wide Rust fast lane targets <=90 seconds; timing is reported with test/pass counts and cannot be achieved by silently omitting named behavioral coverage.
- Slow production-capacity, full-mission, privacy, provenance, and long-determinism checks have explicit milestone/release commands and triggers; they do not run on every slice.
- The seven genuine Level 2 C-ABI failures observed at the audit revision are fixed through production behavior or remain honestly blocking. Their assertions are not loosened or deleted.
- Current Unity Level 2 qualification no longer depends on the frozen historical 31-test registry or exact total test counts. Historical Level 1 receipts remain archival and revision-bound.
- Active package/cache gates validate schemas, versions, content, and semantic closure rather than unrelated source-file or self-referential receipt hashes.
- AGENTS.md and the nearest operator docs state exact commands, cadence, proof class, and the No-Claim boundary for each tier.
- A separate verifier reviews all gate/test changes for weakening and reruns the accepted commands at the exact integrated revision before closure.

## No-Claim
A green fast lane does not prove the full Level 1 preservation release, long-run determinism, production-capacity event retention, built-player privacy, public-boundary safety, or successor asset compatibility. Those claims require their named milestone/release controls.

## Retirement condition
This epic closes after the integrated lean cadence is independently verified and becomes the canonical development route. No continuing audit dashboard or meta-tracker survives it; the executable tests and concise commands are the durable output.
close_reason: All executable lean-gate leaves and independent verification are complete. Canonical tiered cadence is in AGENTS.md; current Level 2 Rust/C-ABI/Unity lanes are green, slow/release controls remain explicit, historical PLAN29 is archival, and no Blender gate or continuing audit dashboard was introduced. Return to playable Level 1/2 implementation.

title: [LEAN-RUST] Tier soak-scale Rust tests and replace blanket Clippy
description:
## Positive outcome
Make the ordinary Rust development lane fast and high-signal without deleting or weakening production-capacity coverage. Separate the two audit-identified soak-scale sim-capi tests from the default lane, and replace the unusable all-targets/all-pedantic Clippy command with a focused correctness-oriented lint gate for changed production code.

## Observed defects
At audit revision 7b3937f, cargo test --workspace --locked took about 484 seconds. bounded_event_journal_reports_expired_cursors drives more than 4,096 full session steps, and presentation_frame_abi_is_revisioned_complete_idempotent_and_fail_closed spans roughly 1,900 lines and combines many concerns. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings produced 1,272 diagnostics dominated by similar_names, test size, bounded casts, and missing docs rather than new correctness defects.

## Allowed scope
- research/private/remc2-sim-rs workspace/Cargo lint configuration
- crates/sim-capi test code and test-only helpers needed to parameterize the two named slow tests
- concise Rust test-cadence documentation adjacent to the workspace
Do not change gameplay semantics, public C ABI layout, Level 1 conformance data, owner assets, Unity code, or unrelated style.

## Required behavior
- Keep a fast discriminating event-journal expiration test using a deliberately small injected/test-only capacity or equivalent production-faithful mechanism.
- Keep the real production-capacity 4,096-event check separately runnable as a named soak/milestone test.
- Split the presentation-frame mega-test into focused ABI/fail-closed/idempotency checks and an explicitly named slow rendering/coverage tier, or otherwise prove a comparable fast/slow separation.
- Define an exact focused Clippy command that treats correctness/suspicious defects as hard failures without requiring a bulk cleanup of existing pedantic test style.

title: Design the successor mountains, forests, volcano, atmosphere, and weather contract
description:
## Purpose

## Evidence questions

## Required decisions
- Mountains: terrain constraints, traversal landmarks, collision/visibility and tactical purpose.
- Trees/forests: authored distribution, instancing/culling, collision, fire/damage policy, AI queries, provenance and response to terrain deformation.
- Volcano: static landmark versus authoritative timed eruption; warning, projectiles/hazard radius, terrain effect, lava presentation, damage and reset.
- Weather: server-owned phase/seed and gameplay effects versus client-local rain/cloud/fog/audio; transition timing, visibility, projectile/flight/AI impact, accessibility reductions and late-join state.
- Authority: classify every value as canonical simulation, replicated event/state, deterministic presentation seed or local quality choice.

## Acceptance criteria
- MC1/MC2 differences and the absence/presence of true dynamic weather are explicitly evidenced.
- Demo contract uses one mountainous volcanic island, forest/tree clusters and one clear-to-storm transition.
- Default demo scope is a bounded authoritative eruption hazard with no fluid-lava simulation, and synchronized mostly-presentational weather with no hidden gameplay penalty unless Oliver expands it.
- Synthetic environment scenarios define state, transitions, networking, save/load, replay and failure artifacts.
- WebGL2 budgets cover terrain silhouette, trees, clouds/fog/rain, ash/plume, lava/emissives, particles, audio and lighting.

title: Map authoritative house impacts to bounded cell damage and visible breaches
description:
## Outcome
Turn a source-authoritative Level 1 house damage occurrence into deterministic local cell damage that creates a visible wall/roof breach without changing gameplay damage.

## Algorithm contract
Transform the authoritative impact position into manifest-local coordinates using the house anchor. Select affected cells by material response, bounded radius and stable distance/ID tie-break. If an older damage path lacks a position, choose a documented deterministic facade point from attacker-to-house direction and event ordinal. Damage amount is calibrated from the source occurrence but never feeds back into HouseState.

## Content behavior
A nonlethal hit can create a local hole and reveal the declared room/furniture behind it. Windows/openings remain intentional empty space. Repeated hits expand the same breach predictably. Cap pressure yields a stable coarse fracture, not unbounded work.

## Tests
Golden streams cover edge hit, roof hit, window near-miss, local hole/no collapse, repeated hits, two equal-distance tie cases, missing-position fallback, cap pressure and reset. Assert exact damaged-cell IDs/hashes and unchanged source house life/terrain/collision outputs versus mode-off.

title: Implement deterministic support, mass, center-of-mass, and collapse classification
description:
## Outcome
After cell damage, recompute bounded support components and classify each disconnected component as retained, shed, topple or collapsed, producing at most the frozen number of major clusters.

## Model
Mass is cell volume times versioned density_kg_m3 using deterministic integer/rational arithmetic. Compute stable component IDs, mass, center of mass, coarse inertia, support footprint and a versioned stability decision. Sort traversals and equal cases by stable ID. Preserve mass within a declared integer tolerance. Over-cap graphs choose a conservative deterministic coarse cluster.

## Boundary
This classification is VoxelMode presentation-detail authority only. It does not change source collision, terrain or house removal timing. Unity/PhysX may animate the emitted clusters but cannot alter their membership or feed transforms back into Rust gameplay.

## Tests
Fixtures cover fully supported, partial support, detached wall, roof shed, center-of-mass edge stability, topple, symmetric tie, mixed materials, exact mass conservation, maximum clusters and overload. Repeated runs and platform-independent serialization produce identical component/cluster hashes.
close_reason: Integrated main commits a32f599 (isolated c090f95) and 1802119 (isolated 3dbff37). Added renderer-free deterministic face-connected component analysis with fixed-point density x cell-volume mass, integer center of mass, diagonal coarse inertia, support X/Z footprint, stable component/report SHA-256, Supported/Detached/Topple classes, Standing/ShedDetached/Topple/Collapse/CoarseFracture decisions, and a frozen 12-cluster cap. State identity/generation is fail-closed; no gameplay/HouseState/collision/ABI/Unity mutation.
