## Outcome
Define the deterministic provider-neutral boundary through which gameplay queries, edits, streams, hashes, saves, replays and repairs a world without depending on heightfield, bounded-cell, full-voxel, fracture or SDF internals.

## Architecture direction
Use docs/world-representation-backends.md. MC2 selects a deformable 2.5D heightfield provider. Optional local structure cells and a future Minecraft-like volumetric chunk world are parallel providers behind one capability envelope, not branches inside one heightfield implementation.

## Owned output
Versioned provider/capability manifest plus interfaces and conformance fixtures for coordinate conversion, point/surface/solid/material queries, ray/sweep tests, provider-specific edit commands, affected bounds, stable region IDs, streaming lifecycle, collision/nav invalidation, canonical hashes, snapshots/deltas, replay, late join, repair, migration, authority rejection, resource budgets and presentation notices.

Do not implement a production terrain provider, full voxel world, city system, renderer mesh/collider authority, universal edit operation, or voxel work on the MC2 demo critical path.

## Acceptance criteria
- A tiny heightfield adapter and tiny volumetric-cell adapter satisfy the same shared query/hash/snapshot/replay fixture where their declared capabilities overlap.
- Heightfield, bounded-cell, full-volume voxel and authored-fracture providers declare capabilities explicitly; unsupported operations fail explicitly and deterministically.
- Provider ID/schema/state-codec and capability vector bind map, save, replay and room compatibility.
- Flight, projectile, actor, network, save and presentation code cannot access provider-owned arrays, Unity terrain, meshes or colliders.
- Ordering, numeric precision, quantization, bounds, idempotency, streaming states, migration, cancellation, overload and thread ownership are defined.
- Unit/property/golden/replay tests compare shared results and prove provider-specific commands stay inside the common command envelope.
- Failures report contract/provider/version, command, seed/tick, region/query/edit, expected/actual result and affected hash.

title: Define the adaptive score, musical grammar, silence, and browser audio plan
description:
## Purpose
Give the world an original musical identity while preserving space for wind, surf, creatures, spells and silence.

## Work
Define an original instrument and harmonic palette, faction and world motifs, dynamic stems, transition rules, stingers, intensity curves and silence policy. Separate shared world phase from player-local danger so co-op and PvP mixes remain intelligible. Cover serenity, exploration, first possession, stronghold growth, carrier danger, rival contact, storm, eruption, equilibrium, defeat and victory.

## Acceptance criteria
- A cue sheet maps every demo phase and important game state to musical behavior, including when no music should play.
- The music director uses hysteresis, cooldowns and priority so it does not thrash as threats enter and leave.
- Score ducks around critical gameplay cues and conveys no essential information by itself.
- Browser-supported stems, scheduling, compression, voice count, memory, download and loop boundaries are budgeted and tested conceptually.
- The plan includes original composition, performance and sample provenance plus replacement rights.
- At least three short style sketches are compared against the creative pillars before a direction is frozen.

2. Write the finite family/action branch table for this packet and implement only unresolved rows.

- [ ] Duplicate/no-overlap/full-hand/no-free-slot negatives are non-mutating except source-specified state.

- Exercises low/high flight, acceleration, strafe, roll, turning, terrain proximity, collision, knockback, falling, respawn, storm, Fireball, targeting, map/HUD, audio and haptics.

- Stop/rollback rules protect users; the cohort may reject VR or specific locomotion modes.

title: Trace MC2 carrier reservation, routing, cargo, loss, and replacement
description:
## Outcome
Recover carrier spawn counts, reservation, target choice, route/altitude behavior, pickup, cargo, delivery, capacity handling, damage, loss, re-release, replacement, and stuck recovery. Output independent logistics contract and traces. Verify contested mana, full castle, terrain change, destruction, owner death, and simultaneous claims.

## Worker contract

title: Freeze the full MC2 fidelity target, module manifest, and deviation ledger
description:
## Outcome
Freeze exact behavioral parity targets for the complete owned GOG MC2 game, not a selected homage subset. The one-island demo is a separately enumerated milestone slice of the same versioned MC2 module.

## Ledger
For every evidenced MC2 flight, camera, aim, health/death, mana, possession, stronghold/carrier, settlement, objective/exit, spell family and tier, creature, rival, realm, progression, terrain/environment, HUD/map/message, audio/music cue, save/checkpoint, and multiplayer row, record exact build/source, observation, confidence, unknowns, independent contract/vectors, module schema/ID, status, and deviation.

## Rules
Unknown may remain UNKNOWN but may not become silently omitted. A waiver records player impact, evidence gap, owner, expiry/retest, browser/server effect, and Oliver approval. Engine code may not hard-code MC2 catalog rows. Replacement expression and an optional owned-data adapter remain separate.
acceptance_criteria: The exact MC2 build is hash-identified; demo and full-module manifests are separate; every evidenced catalog/realm row is baseline, unknown, implemented, intentionally modernized, or explicitly waived; all MC2 content lives behind the module contract; no MC1 row or silent curated subset remains.
notes:
## Accepted direction 2026-07-23
- MC2 is the primary fidelity lens.
- First target is an utterly similar-feeling noncommercial homage, then evidence-based modernization.
- Preserve mechanic roles and tier/progression relationships closely while all names, assets, maps, prose, UI expression, music, and code remain original or separately licensed.
- Target one shareable approximately 20-minute island first; solo/co-op versus AI and PvP use the same authoritative faction simulation with distinct presets.
- Visual style remains open, with romantic flying-carpet/Aladdin-like wonder as a mood reference only.
- Deviations require a ledger entry and a player-facing, legal/provenance, accessibility, performance, or multiplayer rationale.

title: Add an official NYC Manhattan CityPack provider adapter

title: Build a no-mission Shinjuku free-flight and Fireball sandbox
description:
## Outcome
Deliver the requested no-mission city sandbox: spawn over the accepted Shinjuku CityPack, fly freely through a bounded city circle, shoot Fireballs at city surfaces, and reset instantly.

## Work
- Load CityPack visual and canonical collision/surface payloads through the provider-neutral world seam.
- Add one fixed spawn, one safe reset action, the existing original carpet controls/camera/aim, the first original Fireball-family attack, and a toggleable metre/carpet/human-height scale overlay.
- Fireballs use canonical swept collision and produce a bounded original impact effect or scorch marker. They do not damage buildings in this slice.
- Exercise street-canyon flight, roof skimming, high-speed boundary approach, tile load/unload, building impacts, water impacts, and restart.
- Keep simulation independent from visible mesh freshness.
- No mission, objectives, AI, enemies, mana economy, pickups, strongholds, multiplayer, interiors, structural destruction, rubble, MC2 Level 1 data, or preservation-track integration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A clean native build and the declared browser tier enter free flight without editor-only setup.
- Fixed captures and ruler checks prove the carpet and Fireball are at the intended size relative to road widths, storeys, roofs, towers, and the playable-circle diameter; 0.01x and 100x packs are rejected.
- The player cannot pass through canonical city blockers under the supported speed envelope.
- Fireballs hit the same stable surface IDs in headless query replay, native, and browser runs.
- Visual LOD swaps, delayed visual tiles, and warm versus cold cache do not change collision or Fireball outcomes.
- Leaving the playable circle gives a clear boundary response and reset always returns to a valid spawn.
- Missing visual tiles with collision present degrade visibly but safely; missing or mismatched canonical collision rejects the pack.
- A five-minute scripted free-flight soak records load time, frame-time tails, memory, stalls, query mismatches, projectile count, and pooled-effect cleanup with no unbounded growth.

## Test plan
Headless query replay, native free flight, browser free flight, cold/warm load, delayed and missing visual tile, collision mismatch rejection, high-speed wall approach, roof skim, water shot, repeated Fireball impacts, circle boundary, known-speed 100 m travel, scale-overlay capture, deliberate 0.01x and 100x package rejection, 100 resets, and deterministic query-trace comparison.

title: Epic: prove licensed CityPack ingestion and a Shinjuku pilot
description:
## Outcome
Turn this item into the Track S CityPack ingestion epic. Produce a provider-neutral, provenance-complete package contract and one measured Shinjuku pilot before the destructive city-block integration begins. This non-destructive lane does not require a volumetric-world provider.

## Delivery sequence
1. Freeze source and rights decisions.
2. Freeze CityPack v1 and a wholly synthetic fixture.
3. Implement deterministic validation.
4. Prove a Linux-friendly PLATEAU acquisition and radius clip.
5. Normalize coordinates, stable IDs, and source revisions.
6. Calibrate physical scale against the carpet, streets, buildings, camera, and flight speed.
7. Bake visual LOD tiles and separate canonical collision and Fireball surface-query payloads.
8. Assemble and benchmark one Shinjuku pilot.
9. Add Bern and Manhattan only as optional provider adapters after the core works.

## Boundaries
Track S only. Implementation belongs in the separately provisioned successor repository. This private lab owns planning and provenance review, not successor runtime code. Do not use MC2 code, data, names, maps, or owner-derived assets. Do not scrape proprietary map or photogrammetry services. Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles may be a visual benchmark only and cannot be an ingest, offline, extraction, or bake source. Do not promise photorealistic textures, interiors, or universal destruction from source city geometry.

## Success Criteria
Close when the core children through the Shinjuku pilot are accepted. Bern and Manhattan adapters are optional follow-on siblings and do not block the first city-block proof.

title: Decide approved city sources and rights for Shinjuku, Bern, and Manhattan
description:
## Outcome

## Work

- Evaluate PLATEAU Shinjuku first, swisstopo data for Bern, and official NYC 3D/building data for Manhattan. Record OSM only as a separately licensed fallback layer.
- Mark Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles and any similar service as benchmark-only unless its current terms explicitly permit offline extraction and rebaking; current policy expectation is reject for ingestion.
- Freeze the exact source receipt fields consumed by fetch and validate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The matrix gives PROCEED, LIMIT, or REJECT for each candidate and names the exact Shinjuku primary and fallback.
- Every conclusion links to an official source and records access date and licence/version.
- Texture availability is stated as observed data, never inferred from visual previews.
- Unknown or conflicting terms fail closed and identify the owner or qualified reviewer needed.
- The result makes no legal-clearance claim.

## Test plan
Re-open every primary link, verify one metadata or licence checksum, and run a negative review row with missing attribution and ambiguous derivative rights. The negative row must be rejected with a stable reason.

title: Freeze CityPack v1, provider seams, and a synthetic district fixture
description:
## Outcome
Define the smallest provider-neutral CityPack v1 that can describe a circular city extract without coupling runtime code to PLATEAU, swisstopo, NYC, Unity scenes, or a proprietary service.

## Contract
Specify a versioned package containing source receipts and attribution; CRS and geodetic origin; canonical source-metres-to-runtime-units mapping; local metre coordinates and axes; requested playable radius and visual buffer; immutable source revision; stable parcel/building/road/water IDs; hierarchical tile bounds and LODs; separate visual, canonical collision, semantic, interaction, and optional structural references; hashes; budgets; and migration rules. Define fetch, bake, inspect, and validate command contracts with deterministic exit codes and JSON diagnostics.

Create a wholly original tiny fixture with sloped ground, two roads, water, three buildings, one courtyard, one selected-interaction building, and deliberate malformed variants. Use a small test circle so tests never need network access.

## Boundaries
No real-city download, Unity scene, MC2 input, interiors, destructible simulation, provider-specific fields in the core schema, or fixed promise that one kilometre is affordable. Radius and buffer are explicit inputs; measured gates set production values.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A clean fixture bake repeated twice has identical normalized manifest, feature, and package hashes.
- Stable IDs survive file ordering, material rebakes, and non-semantic source metadata changes.
- CRS, units, origin, bounds, licences, missing payloads, and incompatible revisions fail explicitly.
- The synthetic fixture contains known 1 m, 10 m, and 100 m baselines plus a human-height proxy so scale can be audited without a real-city download.
- Visual LOD changes cannot change canonical collision or interaction IDs.
- The contract explains how provider adapters remain replaceable.

## Test plan
Golden round trip plus malformed licence, CRS, axis, duplicate ID, out-of-circle feature, dangling payload, hash mismatch, path traversal, cap excess, and incompatible schema cases.

title: Prove Linux PLATEAU acquisition and circular Shinjuku clipping
description:
## Outcome
Prove one reproducible Linux-friendly acquisition path from the approved Shinjuku PLATEAU release to a bounded raw-source cache and source receipt. Do not make the PLATEAU Unity SDK a prerequisite.

## Work
- Pin the exact Shinjuku dataset, converter/tool versions, centre coordinate, CRS transformation, and source checksums selected by the rights decision.

- Clip by geometry intersection while retaining source IDs and enough neighbouring geometry to avoid edge cracks.
- Store downloaded raw data outside Git and make the committed test path use a tiny licensed excerpt only if redistribution is approved; otherwise use metadata plus the synthetic fixture.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A dry run reports exact URLs, expected bytes when available, licence, cache target, and transformations without downloading.

## Test plan
Dry run, cold fetch, warm cache, interrupted resume, checksum mismatch, unavailable source, wrong CRS, circle-edge feature, and missing-attribution cases.

title: Normalize Shinjuku source geometry into deterministic CityPack tiles
description:
## Outcome
Convert the approved clipped Shinjuku source into provider-neutral local-metre features and hierarchical CityPack tiles with stable identities.

## Work
- Reproject once from the recorded source CRS to a declared geodetic anchor and local coordinate frame.
- Normalize building, parcel, road, water, terrain, and appearance references without losing source provenance.
- Assign stable IDs from provider, source revision, source feature identity, and documented semantic keys; do not derive identity from array order or mesh output.
- Clean invalid rings, duplicate vertices, winding, degenerate geometry, and tile-edge splits through deterministic rules with before/after counts.
- Preserve a migration map when a source revision changes semantic identity.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Two clean normalizations produce identical semantic hashes and feature/tile membership.
- Reordered input files and appearance-only changes preserve semantic IDs.
- Every source feature is imported, clipped with a recorded reason, or rejected with a stable diagnostic.
- Tile seams have no unowned geometry and bounds enclose every payload.
- Absolute coordinate magnitude never reaches the runtime presentation layer.
- One source metre remains one normalized local metre within the frozen tolerance, and exported bounds carry no hidden scale transform.

## Test plan
Synthetic golden cases plus the pinned Shinjuku clip; input reorder, source-revision change, antimeridian-not-applicable guard, invalid polygon, duplicate ID, tile-edge split, vertical datum metadata, and hash migration cases.

title: Bake Shinjuku visual LOD tiles with source textures and fantasy fallback materials
description:
## Outcome
Bake runtime-ready visual tiles from normalized CityPack geometry while keeping appearance replaceable and independent from gameplay collision.

## Work
- Generate at least near, mid, and far visual LODs with deterministic geometry simplification and tile-edge handling.
- Preserve approved source appearance textures when present and redistributable. When absent, use an original fantasy material grammar keyed by semantic building classes; do not fabricate photographic detail.
- Atlas or batch materials within configurable browser and native budgets, record texture colour space and channels, and emit content hashes.
- Keep visual mesh, collider, semantic, and interaction identities linked only through stable IDs.
- Produce preview cameras and an inspect report for silhouette, holes, normals, z-fighting, tile seams, material count, triangles, texture bytes, and draw batches.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Repeated bakes have identical semantic geometry and material-recipe hashes.
- Missing or forbidden textures cleanly select the original fallback path.
- LOD swaps preserve building silhouettes and never change collision or interaction payloads.
- Every material and texture has a provenance row and redistribution decision.
- Deliberate budget excess fails before packaging with the largest contributors named.

## Test plan
Synthetic textured/untextured cases, the approved Shinjuku clip, bad UVs, missing texture, forbidden source texture, non-manifold input, LOD seam, atlas overflow, colour-space mismatch, and repeat-bake comparison.

title: Derive CityPack canonical collision and Fireball surface queries
description:
## Outcome
Derive the minimum engine-neutral gameplay payloads needed to fly through the normalized pilot and shoot Fireballs at city surfaces: conservative canonical collision plus deterministic surface-hit semantics.

## Work
- Derive terrain, building, roof, wall, water, bridge, and restricted-volume collision from normalized semantic geometry, never from the currently visible LOD mesh.
- Emit stable surface IDs and material categories sufficient for carpet sweeps, projectile rays or sweeps, impact normals, water hits, and optional cosmetic scorch placement.
- Define one validated spawn volume and safe reset point inside the playable circle.
- Record simplification error and conservative collider inflation separately from visual LOD.
- Keep navigation, AI, missions, objectives, economy, interiors, interaction graphs, structural supports, destruction cells, and rubble out of this slice.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Identical normalized input produces identical collider, surface, spawn, and query-result hashes.
- Visual rebakes and LOD timing cannot change carpet or projectile query results.
- The spawn and reset volumes are clear of canonical collision and inside the playable circle.
- Unsupported geometry fails closed or becomes a named conservative blocker; it never silently disappears.
- Every projectile impact resolves to a stable surface ID, point, normal, and material category.
- Collider complexity and query cost are measured and budgeted independently from rendering.

## Test plan
Synthetic goldens and pinned Shinjuku cases for street canyons, roofs, overhangs, courtyards, water, sloped roads, thin towers, tile seams, high-speed carpet sweeps, projectile tunnelling, spawn clearance, reset, visual-only rebuild, and malformed references.

Actual normalized city collision, water/bridge/restricted surfaces, LOD/cache invariance, and soak evidence remain open.

title: Calibrate CityPack world scale against carpet, streets, and buildings
description:
## Outcome
Freeze and automatically verify the physical scale from geospatial source metres through CityPack local coordinates, runtime world units, carpet dimensions, camera, collision, and Fireball presentation. Prevent a technically valid city import from making the player appear ant-sized or giant-sized.

## Work
- Declare the canonical conversion, preferably one runtime world unit equals one metre, and record every source-unit, CRS, vertical-datum, model-import, and engine transform.
- Freeze original successor reference dimensions for carpet span and length, rider or eye height, Fireball diameter, collision clearance, camera near plane, and supported flight-speed range.
- Select source-grounded Shinjuku checks spanning a doorway or storey proxy where available, one road width, one building footprint, one building height, a 10 m baseline, a 100 m baseline, and the playable-circle radius.
- Add a headless scale audit and an in-world diagnostic overlay with metre ruler, human-height proxy, carpet envelope, Fireball envelope, building dimensions, local origin, and distance-to-boundary.
- Verify camera FOV and motion cues separately so a correct physical scale is not made to look miniature or enormous.
- Reject hidden FBX or glTF centimetre conversion, double CRS scaling, transform hierarchy scale, and non-uniform runtime scale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A source metre round-trips through normalized CityPack coordinates and runtime placement within the frozen tolerance, with no accumulated scale transform.
- Sample road, footprint, height, and distance measurements agree with approved source metadata or geometry within declared tolerances.
- The carpet, rider proxy, Fireball, door or storey proxy, and streets read at the intended relative size in fixed diagnostic captures.
- Flying 100 m and crossing the pilot diameter take the expected time for the recorded speed profile within deterministic tick tolerance.
- 0.01x, 0.1x, 10x, 100x, non-uniform, and double-origin transforms fail with stable diagnostics before packaging or world load.
- Visual meshes and canonical colliders report the same bounds in metres at every LOD.
- The scale audit runs in CI with the synthetic fixture and in the Shinjuku pilot evidence.

## Test plan
Unit conversion goldens; CRS-to-local round trip; centimetre/metre and millimetre/metre traps; nested transform scale; non-uniform scale; 10 m and 100 m rulers; known building dimensions; fixed FOV captures; known-speed travel timing; LOD bounds comparison; and deliberate 0.01x/100x package rejection.

Source-grounded road/footprint/height/timing checks and actual Shinjuku pilot evidence remain open.

title: Implement semantic building supports and bounded structural failure
description:

Add a deterministic game-structural layer over volumetric or authored building truth: foundations, floors, columns, walls, cores, connections, material capacities, support roots and bounded local failure propagation.

title: Implement multiscale collapse and aggregate rubble-flow fields
description:
## Outcome
Convert authoritative collapse mass into a bounded combination of major collision clusters and an aggregate rubble field that can travel downhill, follow street channels, pile against obstacles, enter water and settle into persistent gameplay collision.

## Non-goals
No authoritative body per brick, unbounded granular particles, cosmetic VFX ownership or fluid-dynamics claim.

## Acceptance criteria
- Mass/volume accounting, stable IDs, flow/settling order, merge/split, obstacle interaction, water handoff and final occupancy are deterministic within declared tolerances.
- A sloped synthetic street fixture proves flow, blockage, ramp formation, save/reload and replay.
- Cosmetic chunks, dust and particles may vary without changing canonical hashes.
- Caps cover active clusters, aggregate cells, work per tick, persistence bytes and network correction.
- Overload conserves gameplay-relevant blockage and settles safely without OOM, divergence or endless motion.

title: Implement voxel-world destruction interest, late join, and repair
description:
## Outcome
Extend the authoritative session protocol for streamed volumetric edits: region interest, accepted operations, acknowledgements, hashes, compact checkpoints, ordered deltas, reconnect, late join, correction, repair and persistent aftermath.

## Non-goals
Do not replicate generated meshes, every fragment, client-computed damage or a second general networking stack.

## Acceptance criteria
- Loss, duplication, reorder, delay, interest entry/exit, unload/reload, reconnect and version mismatch converge or fail explicitly.
- Checkpoints and deltas obey gate-approved bandwidth, snapshot, decode, memory and repair budgets.
- A client cannot edit unloaded/unauthorized regions or exploit stale interest.
- Region/root hashes detect first divergence and bounded repair restores canonical state.
- Twenty-minute multi-client edit soak leaves bounded queues, logs, snapshots and memory.

title: Prove carpet flight, projectiles, and AI across destructive voxel chunks
description:
## Outcome
Prove high-speed carpet movement, aiming, projectiles, visibility and representative ground/flying AI consume only provider-neutral queries while voxel chunks stream, edit, remesh, unload and repair.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests cross positive/negative chunk seams at maximum supported speed and exercise ray/sweep/material queries during edits and delayed presentation rebuilds.
- Canonical collision never depends on visible mesh freshness.
- Ground navigation invalidates bounded regions rather than globally rebuilding; flying navigation handles new openings and closures.
- Native/server/Chrome replay hashes agree under the frozen workload.
- Failures capture provider/build, seed/tick, trajectory, chunk/edit stream, first divergent query/hash, queue depths and profile.

title: Build and validate one streamed destructible city-block module
description:
## Outcome
Build one original or properly licensed streamed city-block game module: several streets, height variation, water edge where useful, multiple buildings, carpet flight, Fireball damage, structural failure, rubble flow, persistence and multiplayer.

## Acceptance criteria
- Source manifests, licenses, attribution and transformations are complete; a synthetic fallback can run the test without proprietary services.
- The exact flat-screen native/server/Chrome build proves cold/warm streaming, flight, combat, simultaneous edits, one bounded collapse, rubble settling, save/reload, late join, reconnect and repair.
- Visual LOD changes do not alter authoritative openings, collision or settled obstacles.
- Typical, P95, maximum-supported and deliberate-overload runs meet the authorized caps or fail closed with the first breached metric.
- A 20-minute mixed-AI/multiplayer soak leaves bounded memory, queues, snapshots, traffic and world deltas.

title: Gate: accept or reject expansion beyond one destructible city block
description:
## Outcome
Accept, limit or reject expansion from the bounded city-block proof to larger streamed destructive districts and recognizable cities.

## Acceptance criteria
- Review gameplay value, comfort/readability, source rights, authoring throughput, deterministic truth, structural/rubble credibility, persistence, networking, Chrome/native/server performance, accessibility, safety and operations.
- Freeze exact world/player/destruction/streaming caps and the next validation rung.
- REJECT is a valid pass and leaves MC2, bounded destruction and the generic world-provider seam intact.
- No promise of all-city brick simulation or production real-city coverage is made without measured evidence.

title: Implement the demo caldera area-controller role
description:
## Outcome
Implement the demo caldera area-controller role. Deliver one bounded, versioned subsystem or artifact; adjacent systems remain non-goals.

## Acceptance contract
- Inputs and authoritative owner are explicit.
- Focused plain-.NET/native/WebGL/server tests cover the named behavior as applicable.

title: Plan repository architecture, CI/CD, release engineering, and dependencies
description:
## What
Define a reproducible development and release system before git init or Unity project creation.

## Scope
Public/private repo ownership; code license; Unity serialization/meta files; assembly boundaries; large assets; formatting/analyzers; branching/review; package manifests/lockfiles; editor/modules; deterministic fixtures; build artifacts/symbols/replays; secrets; dependency provenance/SBOM; vulnerability updates; release signing; and rollback.

## Acceptance criteria
- Repository layout and public/private boundaries match the provenance plan.
- CI lanes are specified for PR, nightly, milestone, and release.
- Lanes cover pure simulation tests, WebGL2/native/server builds, integration/content validation, 2-4 client headless scenarios, browser console errors, headers/cache/CORS, chaos, soak, and min-hardware manual certification.
- Browser artifacts use immutable build IDs with correct MIME/compression/cache policy.
- Third-party code/assets have license, version, provenance, vulnerability, update, and removal records.
- No platform is advertised without native/runtime verification.
- A clean environment can reproduce each supported artifact.

title: Execute WebGL2 terrain, memory, AOT, and frame-budget stress gate
description:
## Outcome
Prove the baseline browser can sustain the core terrain workload without relying on WebGPU.

## Acceptance criteria
- Tier-1 browsers on minimum hardware execute representative travel, spell, continuous-deformation, chunk-stream, save/load, and suspend/resume scenarios.
- Budgets cover download, startup, heap growth/peak, allocations/GC, CPU slices, frame pacing, terrain latency, shader variants, and crash/out-of-memory behavior.
- AOT/reflection/link stripping smoke tests exercise every shared serialization/message path.
- Work is bounded per frame and overload degrades visibly and safely rather than desynchronizing.
- Browser console, mapped stacks, build ID, profiler capture, replay, state hashes, and memory timeline are retained.
- Gate returns pass, reduce scope/quality, redesign, or stop.

title: Ghidra campaign: main loop, timing, numerics, RNG, and entity scheduling
description:
## Questions
Trace startup into the main update loop; timer/fixed-step behavior; input sampling boundaries; coordinate/fixed/floating representations; trigonometry/lookup tables; clamping/overflow; RNG streams; entity containers; update ordering; and save/network tick relationships.

## Acceptance criteria
- End-to-end main-loop/control-flow map with version applicability and confidence exists.
- Timing and numeric hypotheses are correlated against DOSBox observations.
- RNG and update-order conclusions distinguish fact, strong inference, and unknown.
- Independently written simulation invariants, numeric ranges, diagrams, and synthetic vectors are produced.
- No raw decompilation or original addresses enter public artifacts.

title: Epic: original commercial carpet-world successor preproduction
description: Track S only. Define and approve an original commercial carpet-flight game: browser social demo first, authoritative solo/co-op/PvP/AI, deformable island, original art/audio/text, Unity baseline with measured browser gate, Blender pipeline, later native OpenXR and streamed destructible-city vertical slice. MC2/remc2 are not implementation dependencies. Acceptance: current governing documents, independently authored scope, stack proof plan, provenance isolation, actionable acyclic implementation DAG, and Oliver approval.
notes:
## Refinement log

### Pass 1 - idea generation and ruthless scope cut
Generated a broad candidate set, then retained the 15 highest-leverage planning areas: product box, clean-room rules, experimental protocol, baseline corpus, flight, terrain, gameplay loop, AI/level laws, simulation contract, terrain and netcode bake-offs, original art/content direction, verification budgets, milestone/kill criteria, and approval gate. Explicitly deferred caves/voxels, seamless world, 8+ players, services, compatibility work, and production art.

### Pass 2 - adversarial architecture review
Corrected fixed-tick versus determinism language; made the server-owned quantized heightfield canonical; kept full terrain out of high-frequency rollback; required predicted kinematic movement rather than canonical PhysX; separated URP/Web client/presentation from headless server; added max-speed interest-management, late-join, persistence, and repair gates.

### Pass 3 - dependency and workflow review
Removed br parent-child edges that incorrectly blocked planning tasks. Made product scope and provenance planning parallel. Added the public-source question index and exact Unity package-pinning task. Verified that baseline capture unlocks parallel analysis tracks and that the feasibility epic is blocked through explicit plan approval.

### Pass 4 - tests, observability, and estimate review
Added planning estimates. Required pure simulation unit/property/golden tests, integration tests, headless end-to-end network chaos tests, visual/performance gates, structured command/state hashes, reproducible failure artifacts, synthetic fixtures, and companion test work for every future implementation feature.

### Pass 5 - provenance, tooling, and initial graph health
Integrated owned-game observation, first-party historical evidence, remc/remc2, MagicBalls, mgcarpet, editors, and format notes as separately license-graded research inputs. Pinned a time-stamped candidate Unity 6.3/URP/Web/NGO/UTP stack for later re-verification. Repaired derived cache state and verified an acyclic actionable graph.

### Pass 6 - browser promoted to Tier 1
Oliver made browser support mandatory. Rejected HDRP because Unity Web does not support it. Revised the single-pipeline candidate to URP, WebGL2 as the required baseline, and experimental WebGPU as optional enhancement. Added browser build/load/memory/input/persistence diagnostics, secure browser-compatible netcode, Linux authoritative server interoperability, and an explicit browser feasibility gate.

### Pass 7 - product, operations, and whole-game coverage
Added decision work for release/business/source licensing, multiplayer player journey and identity, hosting/cost/operations, persistence, browser lifecycle, accessibility and comfort, map tooling, playtesting and ethical telemetry, adversarial QA, CI/release, asset delivery, governance/support, branding/privacy/ratings, original worldbuilding, and resource/hardware ceilings. These are inputs to the milestone/kill-criteria task rather than an unbounded wish list.

### Pass 8 - private-lab boundary and bounded Ghidra campaigns
Replaced the loose clean-room claim with provenance-controlled independent reimplementation language and made legal posture an explicit review question. Added physical separation of proprietary installers/captures/analysis from the future public repository. Split executable study into reproducible lab setup, main-loop/numerics, flight, terrain, gameplay/AI, save/network, and contamination-audit campaigns; all outputs require confidence, synthetic vectors, and independently written specifications.

### Pass 9 - planning versus execution and complete feasibility DAG
Removed acceptance criteria that pretended planning tasks had already executed Unity/browser benchmarks. Added a complete post-approval implementation DAG: toolchain, public skeleton, empty artifact matrix, simulation and test harnesses, flight/terrain/browser/network gates, original game loop/map/art slice, accessibility playtest, public-internet hosting proof, and final evidence decision. Every executable task is transitively blocked by mc-w58.15.

### Pass 10 - graph simplification and adversarial closeout
Collapsed the approval gate's duplicate direct blockers behind the milestone/risk aggregator, Ghidra audit, and feasibility-DAG audit. Required deterministic logs, hashes, seeds, versioned artifacts, browser consoles, profiler captures, chaos/soak evidence, privacy/security negative tests, and explicit cut/redesign/stop outcomes. Final br doctor, cycle check, and bv robot review remain the closeout step.

## Current rule
No Unity installation, Unity project, gameplay code, public repository initialization, or production asset work is authorized until mc-w58.15 is explicitly approved and closed.

### Pass 11 - Oliver decision checkpoint: shared modes, evidence-gated release, Chrome-first bootstrap
Recorded that co-op and PvP use one authoritative simulation/network/terrain foundation but require separately designed rules for teams, resources, death, griefing, pause/disconnect, objectives, matchmaking, moderation, balance, and AI. The feasibility slice must exercise both; launch emphasis is a post-feasibility evidence decision. Deferred permanent business and source-license choice until the slice measures fun, content throughput, hosting burden, and audience, while retaining reversible prototype publication/license guardrails. Narrowed browser certification to current desktop Chrome on Windows/Linux for feasibility; other browsers are compatibility observations/later gates. Replaced fixed staffing/calendar/cash assumptions with an Oliver-plus-Codex bootstrap model, explicit approval for every spend, and unchanged technical/provenance/quality kill criteria.

### Pass 12 - manual-grounded playable-demo and feature-completeness correction
Read and visually checked the owned MC1 and scanned MC2 manuals plus MC2 reference-card controls. MC1 establishes 50 worlds, 24 spells, finite mana/possession, castle/balloon logistics, civilians/towns, rival wizards/network information, 13 documented creature types, terrain/world spells, death/restart, saves, maps/HUD and equilibrium completion (especially MC1 PDF pp.7-20). MC2 establishes 25 serial-objective realms, Fireball/Possession as starting verbs, 25 spell families with three experience tiers, named rival hierarchy, roughly twenty creature roles, day/night and cave/mountain/volcanic environments, saves and 2-8-player network support (MC2 scan PDF pp.4-13 and reference card PDF p.2). Neither manual establishes a general natural-weather simulator or trees as a gameplay system; dynamic storm behavior and tree/deformation rules are explicit modern additions.

The prior DAG could pass independent greybox, art and network labs without one integrated playable artifact. Added a manual-backed completeness ledger; environmental contract; explicit technical-proof gate; Fireball plus four hostile-pressure roles; volcanic mountain/forest/storm implementation; a convergence demo requiring five-plus spell roles, mana possession, vulnerable carrier/stronghold, settlement consequence, objective, HUD, death/restart/save and solo/multiplayer; and separate post-demo vertical-slice and feature-complete-alpha gates. Independent re-reading of the owned MC2 reference card/manual and public manual transcription confirms 2-8 individually identified competitors, same-session setup, selected wizard/colour slots, a preselected network level, no serial campaign progression and no pause. It does not establish network victory, exit, mana quota, friendly fire, death/rebuild or team/co-op rules. Oliver set the destination to a faithful full Magic Carpet 2 reimplementation in Unity/browser, with the one-island friend demo as milestone one rather than final scope. MC1 research/parity beads were removed. The engine is module-neutral and moddable; MC2 is the first complete versioned module. MC2 is now explicitly one replaceable GameModule implementation, never a privileged engine mode. Package kinds cover full game modules, campaign/world packs, rules profiles, presentation/localization packs, and bounded declarative behavior graphs. A synthetic micro-game must prove engine isolation. Chrome, native, Linux authority, rooms, saves and replays bind one canonical engine/simulation/protocol/module/content/profile/rules tuple.

Added 25 per-realm implementation packages, three campaign-arc gates, full progression/save/secret/migration acceptance, a start-to-ending cross-target replay walkthrough, and full Chrome content/cache/memory acceptance. Added a complete MC2 multiplayer-content branch for evidenced network levels, faithful versus modern profiles, 2-8 participant conformance, HUD/lifecycle parity, matrix tests and playtests. title: Plan terrain implementation bake-off and proof gates
description:
## What
Design a disposable comparison between Unity Terrain and custom tiled heightfield presentation, both driven by the same canonical terrain contract.

## Why
Unity Terrain may be adequate or may stall under frequent changes. Custom chunks offer control but add engineering cost. This must be measured before gameplay or art depends on either path.

## Scenarios
Repeated deformation; dirty normals/collision; shoreline changes; structure masks; foliage grounding; TAA; decals; shadows; motion vectors; save/reload; representative world sizes.

## Acceptance criteria
- Minimum hardware, frame, simulation-tick, memory, allocation, and mutation-rate budgets are frozen before the spike.
- The post-approval execution plan includes 10,000 randomized mutations and render/collision agreement within a declared tolerance.
- The plan requires save/load to produce identical canonical chunk hashes and defines failure artifacts.
- Failure actions state when to reject Unity Terrain, custom chunks, world scale, or visual assumptions.

title: Plan custom-protocol networking and authoritative terrain proof
description: Specify a custom versioned command/snapshot protocol with replaceable transports and authority-host adapters. Evaluate Unity Transport 2.7.4 plus NGO 2.13.0 only as adapter candidates, never as the authoritative game model. Include the Unity Dedicated Server versus .NET 10 host bakeoff, secure WebSocket browser path, prediction/reconciliation, quantized terrain edits, late join, repair, reconnect, abuse limits and four-client chaos.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol/schema IDs and compatibility rules are explicit; browser raw-socket restrictions are respected; authority never transfers to clients; same workload runs on both host candidates; 120 ms RTT/20 ms jitter/1% loss and bandwidth/repair/reconnect thresholds match docs/successor-stack-pin.md; pass/fail selects adapters without coupling Simulation.Core to NGO.
notes:
## Current candidate to challenge
Start with NGO 2.13.0 under strict server authority, letting Unity 6.3 UPM resolve and lock the compatible Unity Transport version before testing. NGO anticipation is not complete prediction/reconciliation, so custom predicted kinematic flight remains part of the experiment.

The browser path is mandatory: prove the Unity-supported Web networking transport to a Linux headless server under secure-origin constraints. Native direct/LAN is a secondary transport scenario, not the architecture gate. Netcode for Entities is considered only if measured correction behavior or entity scale fails. Lobby/Matchmaker/commercial hosting remain deferred, but browser reachability may require a minimal deployed endpoint earlier than the native-only plan assumed.

title: Design the behavioral reverse-engineering protocol
description:

design:
Ghidra is first-class but decompiler output is hypothesis evidence, never a transcript. Static conclusions require loader/memory-map validation, instruction/IR/dataflow review, runtime correlation, discriminating external behavior, and stop rules for overlays, packing, self-modification, or mapping ambiguity.

Implementation receives only reviewed fresh-language functional findings, applicability, uncertainty, synthetic vectors, required behavior, and explicit internal freedom. Red payloads never transfer. The v3 original synthetic dry-run proved the packet can be executed by a genuinely fresh low-context worker using pinned source, ENV, TOOL, interpreter and OS identities; it preserved a deliberate INVALID_CONFIRMATORY run, used unique question/hypothesis/experiment/run/evidence IDs, and received fresh independent APPROVE_EVIDENCE review.

title: Write the renderer-independent simulation contract
description:
## What
Specify the authoritative simulation boundary before choosing concrete Unity packages.

## Why
A fixed tick is not the same as determinism, and Unity physics/rendering must not become canonical world state. Clear boundaries allow headless servers, tests, replays, and renderer changes.

## Contract
- Server authority and fixed simulation cadence.
- Kinematic predicted carpet movement; PhysX is not canonical.
- Domain-limited determinism for terrain operations/hashes, seeded generation, resources, spell ordering, persistence, and replay.
- Partitioned RNG streams.
- Versioned serialization and schema migration.
- Presentation-only animation, particles, cloth, and camera effects.

## Acceptance criteria
- Assembly boundaries cover Simulation.Core, Unity adapters, Networking, Terrain Presentation, Client, and Server.
- Core rules can be tested without Unity scenes, render-pipeline code, or presentation/runtime dependencies.
- Headless server never loads presentation assets.
- Rollback scope explicitly excludes canonical full-heightfield copies; terrain uses ordered confirmation, hashes, snapshots, and repair.
notes:
## Provisional language boundary
- Simulation.Core: pure modern C#/.NET with no UnityEngine dependency.
- Unity adapters, client, and headless server bootstrap: C#.
- Rendering and compute: HLSL plus Shader Graph/VFX Graph where they improve iteration.
- Tests: NUnit/Unity Test Framework in C#; black-box orchestration may use Python.
- Reverse engineering: Ghidra/PyGhidra Python and Java APIs, with scripts stored only in the private research lab when they contain original-specific details.
- Rust: optional standalone parsers, corpus tools, or performance experiments only after a measured need. No Rust FFI in the first runtime architecture.

## Rationale
One runtime language keeps IL2CPP/AOT, profiling, debugging, serialization, package integration, and client/server code sharing straightforward. A 2-4-player server-authoritative heightfield game does not need Rust for baseline performance. The simulation assembly boundary preserves the option to port or replace components later without paying cross-language cost on day one.

title: Design and balance the shareable volcanic-atoll demo level and mode variants
description:
## Outcome
Design one original 15-30 minute world that friends can open in Chrome and play as solo-with-AI, fixed-team co-op, adversarial PvP, or mixed human/AI factions while learning the authentic Magic-Carpet-style economy.

## Evidence basis
Compress the original guide's early learning arc: safe flight and the Possess/Castle/Fireball chain; speed and air threats; a weak mana-stealing rival; castle/carrier defense; then an economically competent rival with a castle and balloon. Use MC2's serial-objective clarity and visible exit, but not copied maps, names, scripts, prose, or art. Original MC2 multiplayer was elimination plus exit rather than co-op; fixed factions and co-op are deliberate modern additions.

## Spatial and phase contract
- Four fair outer spawn terraces, a mountain ring, forested settlement basin, shoreline routes, artillery highlands, mana-predator habitat, and a contested volcanic caldera.
- Phase 1: 0-2 minute protected flight/aim sanctuary.
- Phase 2: release, possess, transport, bank, and grow; visibly distinguish neutral, claimed/exposed, reserved, in-transit, secured, spent, and re-released mana.
- Phase 3: defend carrier/stronghold and gain one settlement consequence.
- Phase 4: rival/faction contest, terrain tactic, clear-to-storm presentation.
- Phase 5: telegraphed eruption, central reserve, threshold and exit-control climax.
- Explicit overtime/stalemate resolution; no scavenger-hunt cleanup.

## Modes and faction rules
- Co-op: humans share a faction objective against neutral ecology and an AI rival.
- PvP: FFA or fixed teams use separate faction economies.
- Mixed: humans and AI can occupy fixed factions.
- Lobby membership is locked for the match; mutable diplomacy is excluded from the demo.
- The creature-control spell is not player diplomacy.

## Acceptance criteria
- Map plan names stronghold sites, carrier routes, mana placements, settlement benefit/risk, AI deployment, terrain opportunities, protected/deformable zones, hazard bounds, phase triggers, objective logic, exit, overtime, scoring, recovery, and results.
- At least two viable strategic routes exist: harvest/defend and raid/intercept.
- Five spell roles are enough: attack, possess, stronghold, movement/defense, and terrain.
- Three creature pressures plus one symmetric rival wizard are sufficient.
- Test 55%, 60%, and 65% secured-mana thresholds; choose the lowest that causes a real contest without prolonged cleanup.
- Every rule is labeled canonical inspiration, modernized behavior, or original addition.
- No original level geometry, identifiers, names, scripting, text, or assets are required.
notes:
## Pacing decision 2026-07-22
Tune the first island around a roughly 20-minute normal match. Treat this as a starting hypothesis, not a forced timer: map scale, carpet speed, carrier travel, mana density, rival pressure and objective threshold must produce the duration naturally. Preserve a 15-30 minute acceptance envelope until external playtests narrow it.

3. A closure comment with the exact post-extraction edit ledger for `mc-38gs.1` through `.4`, separating model-owned files from unavoidable shared `mod.rs`/parent edits. That ledger controls actual parallel dispatch.

- Required clips include idle, ground movement, takeoff, flight cycle, bank/turn, attack, hit, death, and landing where feasible, with exact duration/root-motion/event rules.
- Valid and deliberately invalid acceptance fixtures make each rule testable.
- Numeric limits derive from mc-620m and mc-us7t and identify minimum/enhanced tiers.
- Evaluation separates semantic correctness, visual quality, author time, deterministic reproducibility, import fidelity, and browser cost.
- Brief has stable version/hash and public-safe original references only.

title: Add asset provenance manifest and third-party-source gate
description:
## Outcome
Implement the authoritative provenance manifest and fail-closed import/release gate for every source, intermediate, and shipped asset.

## Owned output
A versioned manifest schema, validator, canonical CI command, public-safe fixtures, and release evidence covering stable asset ID, source hash, creator/tool/recipe versions, license or original-work declaration, permitted uses, transformations, generated outputs, review state, and package membership.

## Non-goals
Do not ingest private reference-game assets, infer a license from file presence, permit unreviewed network downloads, or use SBOM presence as proof of asset rights.

## Acceptance criteria
- Unknown, missing, conflicting, revoked, incompatible, or privately sourced provenance fails import and release.
- Every shipped asset is traceable through deterministic intermediate and export hashes to an approved source declaration.
- Original work, public-domain work, permissive third-party work, generated work, and private research references remain distinguishable.
- Validator has focused positive/negative tests and emits JSON/JUnit with asset ID, offending field, source/output hashes, tool versions, and repair guidance.
- mc-wbrs consumes the exact passing manifest hash; changing an asset invalidates prior evidence.
